## Rich Formats

Plain text is the floor, not the ceiling. Obsidian renders these natively — use them to make notes scannable, visual, and precise.

### Callouts

Structured highlights for decisions, warnings, key insights. **Use liberally.**

```markdown
> [!tip] Key Insight
> Context management is the primary bottleneck in multi-agent systems.

> [!warning] Consequences
> Removing this cache invalidates all downstream embeddings.

> [!danger] Known Failure
> Never call this API without rate limiting — see [[lesson-18-mock-live-services-in-tests]].

> [!example] Usage
> ```python
> result = engine.query("semantic search")
> ```

> [!abstract] Summary
> Three-sentence TL;DR of this paper or decision.
```

**All types:** `note`, `abstract`/`summary`/`tldr`, `info`, `tip`/`hint`, `success`/`done`, `question`/`faq`, `warning`/`caution`, `failure`/`missing`, `danger`/`error`, `bug`, `example`, `quote`/`cite`, `todo`

**Foldable:** Add `-` to collapse by default: `> [!warning]- Click to expand`

| Directory | Recommended Callouts |
|-----------|---------------------|
| `decisions/` | `> [!warning]` for consequences, `> [!tip]` for rationale |
| `lessons/` | `> [!danger]` for the mistake, `> [!success]` for the fix |
| `papers/` | `> [!abstract]` for summary, `> [!example]` for key findings |
| `concepts/` | `> [!tip]` for key properties, `> [!example]` for usage |
| `patterns/` | `> [!example]` for code, `> [!warning]` for anti-patterns |

### Mermaid Diagrams

Obsidian renders Mermaid natively in fenced code blocks. Use for architecture, workflows, and relationships.

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Agent] -->|queries| B[Cloud Vault MCP]
    B -->|returns| C[Relevant Notes]
    C -->|injected into| D[Agent Context]
    class A,B,C,D internal-link;
```
````

**Tip:** Add `class NodeName internal-link;` to make nodes clickable vault links.

| Signal | Diagram Type |
|--------|-------------|
| System with 3+ interacting components | `graph TD` (top-down flowchart) |
| Process with sequential steps | `graph LR` (left-right flow) |
| Time-ordered events | `sequenceDiagram` |
| State transitions | `stateDiagram-v2` |
| Timeline/roadmap | `timeline` |

### Math / LaTeX

Obsidian renders MathJax natively. Use for physics, ML, and quantitative papers.

```markdown
Inline: The loss function $L(\theta) = -\sum y_i \log \hat{y}_i$ converges at...

Block:
$$
E = mc^2 \quad \text{and} \quad F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}
$$
```

### Aliases

Alternative names for discoverability. Obsidian autocomplete suggests aliases when linking.

```yaml
---
title: "Context Management"
aliases: ["context engineering", "context window optimization", "prompt context"]
---
```

**When to add aliases:**
- Concept has common abbreviations (RAG, MCP, LLM)
- Topic is known by multiple names in different communities
- Note title uses a specific framing but the concept is broader

### Embeds (Transclusion)

Pull content from one note into another. Keeps notes atomic while composing views.

```markdown
![[note-name]]              # Embed entire note
![[note-name#Heading]]      # Embed one section
![[note-name#^block-id]]    # Embed one paragraph
![[image.png|300]]          # Embed image with width
![[document.pdf#page=3]]    # Embed PDF at specific page
```

**When to embed:** MOCs summarizing key sections, decisions referencing experiment results, patterns showing code from concept notes.

### Heading Links

Deep-link into specific sections of notes. More precise than whole-note links.

```markdown
[[context-management#Key Properties]]     # Link to a heading
[[lesson-04#Prevention]]                  # Link to a section
```

**When to use:** Cross-referencing specific evidence, linking to a particular section of a long note rather than the whole thing.

### Block References

Make any paragraph linkable by adding `^block-id` at the end.

```markdown
The key insight is that context quality matters more than quantity. ^key-insight
```

Then reference from anywhere: `[[context-management#^key-insight]]`

---

## Conventions

# Vault Manifest

**Read this first.** This file tells you where everything lives, where to put your output, and what conventions to follow.

## Directory Map

### Content Directories (where knowledge lives)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming | Required Frontmatter |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|---------------------|
| `concepts/` | Core definitions, frameworks, techniques | Defining a reusable idea, technology, or methodology | `kebab-case.md` (no date prefix) | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `papers/` | Research papers, articles, external sources | Summarizing external research with citations | `kebab-case-descriptive-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) | Recording a choice with context, alternatives, consequences | `YYYY-MM-DD-decision-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns | Documenting a repeatable solution to a recurring problem | `kebab-case-pattern-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results | Testing a hypothesis with method, results, learnings | `YYYY-MM-DD-experiment-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `projects/` | Project-level tracking and plans | Tracking a multi-session effort with goals and status | `YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `lessons/` | Lessons learned from mistakes/discoveries | Capturing something learned the hard way — prevents repeat mistakes | `kebab-case-lesson-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]`, `severity` |

### Workflow Directories (where work happens)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — triage point | Dropping raw ideas, unprocessed content, or agent output that needs classification | Any `.md` name |
| `daily/` | Daily notes, session logs, checkpoints | Recording a session's work, daily standup, or checkpoint | `YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` |
| `sessions/` | Formal session records with structured metadata | Documenting a compound engineering session with metrics | `session-NNN-*.md` |
| `missions/` | Multi-agent coordinated tasks | Orchestrating multiple agents toward a shared goal | `mission-name.md` or dated |
| `retrospectives/` | Post-session analysis | Reviewing what worked, what didn't, and why | `YYYY-MM-DD-retrospective.md` |
| `Agents/` | Agent execution records and walkthroughs | Storing agent run artifacts, traces, walkthroughs | `AgentName/UUID/` subdirs |

### Navigation Directories (how to find things)

| Directory | Purpose | Key Files |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `concepts/MOC-*.md` | Maps of Content — curated topic indexes | 8 MOCs: agentic-ai, quantum-physics, vault-architecture, platform-infrastructure, machine-learning, astrophysics, compound-engineering, safety-alignment |

### Infrastructure Directories (tooling, not content)

| Directory | Purpose | Agent Action |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases (no companion note) | Create spatial maps, architecture diagrams |
| `teleport/` | Cloud-to-local file sync (tasks + results) | Use for cross-environment transfers |
| `docs/` | Long-form documentation, brand guides | Reference only — don't create here without asking |
| `meta/` | Self-recording, compound demos | Specialized — check before writing |
| `specs/` | Formal specifications | For major system designs |
| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/

```

## Quick Start for Agents

### Starting a session:
1. Read this manifest (you're doing it now)
2. Check `inbox/` for items needing triage
3. Load the relevant MOC for your task: `concepts/MOC-*.md`

title: "Vault Manifest — Agent Orientation"
date: 2026-03-04
tags: [manifest, navigation, agent-onboarding]
purpose: Machine-readable vault map for agent session startup
---

# Vault Manifest

**Read this first.** This file tells you where everything lives, where to put your output, and what conventions to follow.

## Directory Map

### Content Directories (where knowledge lives)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming | Required Frontmatter |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|---------------------|
| `concepts/` | Core definitions, frameworks, techniques | Defining a reusable idea, technology, or methodology | `kebab-case.md` (no date prefix) | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `papers/` | Research papers, articles, external sources | Summarizing external research with citations | `kebab-case-descriptive-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) | Recording a choice with context, alternatives, consequences | `YYYY-MM-DD-decision-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns | Documenting a repeatable solution to a recurring problem | `kebab-case-pattern-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results | Testing a hypothesis with method, results, learnings | `YYYY-MM-DD-experiment-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `projects/` | Project-level tracking and plans | Tracking a multi-session effort with goals and status | `YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `lessons/` | Lessons learned from mistakes/discoveries | Capturing something learned the hard way — prevents repeat mistakes | `kebab-case-lesson-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]`, `severity` |

### Workflow Directories (where work happens)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — triage point | Dropping raw ideas, unprocessed content, or agent output that needs classification | Any `.md` name |
| `daily/` | Daily notes, session logs, checkpoints | Recording a session's work, daily standup, or checkpoint | `YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` |
| `sessions/` | Formal session records with structured metadata | Documenting a compound engineering session with metrics | `session-NNN-*.md` |
| `missions/` | Multi-agent coordinated tasks | Orchestrating multiple agents toward a shared goal | `mission-name.md` or dated |
| `retrospectives/` | Post-session analysis | Reviewing what worked, what didn't, and why | `YYYY-MM-DD-retrospective.md` |
| `Agents/` | Agent execution records and walkthroughs | Storing agent run artifacts, traces, walkthroughs | `AgentName/UUID/` subdirs |

### Navigation Directories (how to find things)

| Directory | Purpose | Key Files |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `concepts/MOC-*.md` | Maps of Content — curated topic indexes | 8 MOCs: agentic-ai, quantum-physics, vault-architecture, platform-infrastructure, machine-learning, astrophysics, compound-engineering, safety-alignment |

### Infrastructure Directories (tooling, not content)

| Directory | Purpose | Agent Action |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases (no companion note) | Create spatial maps, architecture diagrams |
| `teleport/` | Cloud-to-local file sync (tasks + results) | Use for cross-environment transfers |
| `docs/` | Long-form documentation, brand guides | Reference only — don't create here without asking |
| `meta/` | Self-recording, compound demos | Specialized — check before writing |
| `specs/` | Formal specifications | For major system designs |
| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

---

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/
I mapped relationships visually        → companion .canvas next to the .md, or canvas/ if standalone
I don't know where this goes          → inbox/     (always safe default)
```

**When in doubt, use `inbox/`.** The vault keeper triages inbox items into their proper location with correct frontmatter and cross-links.

---

## Canvas Files (Multimodal Assets)

**Notes explain. Canvases show.** When a topic has complex relationships, spatial layout reveals structure that prose cannot. Create `.canvas` files alongside their companion `.md` notes.

### When to Create a Canvas

| Signal | Canvas Type |
|--------|-------------|
| MOC with 10+ linked notes | **Relationship map** — nodes for notes, edges for connections |
| Architecture or system design | **Architecture diagram** — groups for layers, text cards for components |
| Decision with 3+ alternatives | **Decision landscape** — cards per option, edges to trade-offs |
| Research cluster spanning domains | **Domain map** — grouped by field, edges for cross-domain links |
| Vault keeper nudges you | The hook detected 10+ outbound links — the note wants a canvas |

### Naming and Placement

Canvas files live **alongside their companion note**:
- `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.md` → `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.canvas`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.md` → `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.canvas`
- Standalone canvases (no companion note) → `canvas/` directory

### JSON Format

Obsidian canvas files are JSON with `nodes` and `edges`:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"unique-id", "type":"file", "file":"concepts/machine-learning.md", "x":0, "y":0, "width":250, "height":60},
    {"id":"label-1",   "type":"text", "text":"## Key Insight\n\nMarkdown content here", "x":300, "y":0, "width":300, "height":120, "color":"4"},
    {"id":"group-1",   "type":"group","label":"ML Cluster", "x":-50, "y":-50, "width":600, "height":250, "color":"2"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id":"edge-1", "fromNode":"unique-id", "toNode":"label-1", "label":"informs"}
  ]
}
```

**Node types:**
- `file` — link to a vault note (opens on click). Use `"file": "path/to/note.md"`
- `text` — inline markdown card. Use `"text": "## Title\n\nContent"`
- `group` — visual grouping box. Use `"label": "Group Name"`

**Colors:** `"1"` red, `"2"` orange, `"3"` yellow, `"4"` green, `"5"` cyan, `"6"` purple, or hex `"#RRGGGG"`

**Layout tips:** Use x/y grid spacing of ~300px horizontal, ~150px vertical. Groups should surround their children with ~50px padding.

---

## Rich Formats

Plain text is the floor, not the ceiling. Obsidian renders these natively — use them to make notes scannable, visual, and precise.

### Callouts

Structured highlights for decisions, warnings, key insights. **Use liberally.**

```markdown
> [!tip] Key Insight
> Context management is the primary bottleneck in multi-agent systems.

> [!warning] Consequences
> Removing this cache invalidates all downstream embeddings.

> [!danger] Known Failure
> Never call this API without rate limiting — see [[lesson-18-mock-live-services-in-tests]].

> [!example] Usage
> ```python
> result = engine.query("semantic search")
> ```

> [!abstract] Summary
> Three-sentence TL;DR of this paper or decision.
```

**All types:** `note`, `abstract`/`summary`/`tldr`, `info`, `tip`/`hint`, `success`/`done`, `question`/`faq`, `warning`/`caution`, `failure`/`missing`, `danger`/`error`, `bug`, `example`, `quote`/`cite`, `todo`

**Foldable:** Add `-` to collapse by default: `> [!warning]- Click to expand`

| Directory | Recommended Callouts |
|-----------|---------------------|
| `decisions/` | `> [!warning]` for consequences, `> [!tip]` for rationale |
| `lessons/` | `> [!danger]` for the mistake, `> [!success]` for the fix |
| `papers/` | `> [!abstract]` for summary, `> [!example]` for key findings |
| `concepts/` | `> [!tip]` for key properties, `> [!example]` for usage |
| `patterns/` | `> [!example]` for code, `> [!warning]` for anti-patterns |

### Mermaid Diagrams

Obsidian renders Mermaid natively in fenced code blocks. Use for architecture, workflows, and relationships.

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Agent] -->|queries| B[Cloud Vault MCP]
    B -->|returns| C[Relevant Notes]
    C -->|injected into| D[Agent Context]
    class A,B,C,D internal-link;
```
````

**Tip:** Add `class NodeName internal-link;` to make nodes clickable vault links.

| Signal | Diagram Type |
|--------|-------------|
| System with 3+ interacting components | `graph TD` (top-down flowchart) |
| Process with sequential steps | `graph LR` (left-right flow) |
| Time-ordered events | `sequenceDiagram` |
| State transitions | `stateDiagram-v2` |
| Timeline/roadmap | `timeline` |

### Math / LaTeX

Obsidian renders MathJax natively. Use for physics, ML, and quantitative papers.

```markdown
Inline: The loss function $L(\theta) = -\sum y_i \log \hat{y}_i$ converges at...

Block:
$$
E = mc^2 \quad \text{and} \quad F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}
$$
```

### Aliases

Alternative names for discoverability. Obsidian autocomplete suggests aliases when linking.

```yaml
---
title: "Context Management"
aliases: ["context engineering", "context window optimization", "prompt context"]
---
```

**When to add aliases:**
- Concept has common abbreviations (RAG, MCP, LLM)
- Topic is known by multiple names in different communities
- Note title uses a specific framing but the concept is broader

### Embeds (Transclusion)

Pull content from one note into another. Keeps notes atomic while composing views.

```markdown
![[note-name]]              # Embed entire note
![[note-name#Heading]]      # Embed one section
![[note-name#^block-id]]    # Embed one paragraph
![[image.png|300]]          # Embed image with width
![[document.pdf#page=3]]    # Embed PDF at specific page
```

**When to embed:** MOCs summarizing key sections, decisions referencing experiment results, patterns showing code from concept notes.

### Heading Links

Deep-link into specific sections of notes. More precise than whole-note links.

```markdown
[[context-management#Key Properties]]     # Link to a heading
[[lesson-04#Prevention]]                  # Link to a section
```

**When to use:** Cross-referencing specific evidence, linking to a particular section of a long note rather than the whole thing.

### Block References

Make any paragraph linkable by adding `^block-id` at the end.

```markdown
The key insight is that context quality matters more than quantity. ^key-insight
```

Then reference from anywhere: `[[context-management#^key-insight]]`

---

## Conventions

### Frontmatter (YAML)

Every note in a content directory MUST have frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: "Note Title"
date: 2026-03-04
tags: [tag1, tag2, tag3]
---
```

**Tags are ALWAYS arrays** — never comma-separated strings.

**Status values by directory:**
- `decisions/`: `proposed` → `accepted` → `deprecated` | `rejected`
- `experiments/`: `in-progress` → `complete` | `failed`
- `projects/`: `active` → `complete` → `archived`

### Cross-References

Use Obsidian wiki-links: `[[note-name]]`

- Use bare filename (no path prefix): `[[machine-learning]]` not `[[concepts/machine-learning]]`
- Link at first mention of a concept
- Every note should have 3+ outbound wiki-links
- Every new note must be linked FROM at least one existing note (no orphans)

### Templates

Directories with `_template.md` files: `decisions/`, `patterns/`, `experiments/`, `projects/`, `daily/`

Copy the template when creating a new note in these directories.

---

## Quick Start for Agents

### Starting a session:
1. Read this manifest (you're doing it now)
2. Check `inbox/` for items needing triage
3. Load the relevant MOC for your task: `concepts/MOC-*.md`
4. Check `lessons/` for past mistakes related to your task

### During your session:
5. Create notes in the correct directory per routing rules above
6. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to connect every new note to 1-3 existing notes
7. Use proper frontmatter with tags as arrays

### Ending a session:
8. Log session summary to `daily/YYYY-MM-DD-session-id.md`
9. If you discovered something reusable, add it to `lessons/` or `patterns/`
10. Any raw output that needs triage → `inbox/`

---

## Vault Health Invariants

A healthy vault maintains:
- **0 orphan notes** in content directories
- **0 frontmatter issues** (missing or malformed)
- **0 broken wiki-links** (pointing to non-existent notes)
- **< 10% thin notes** (under 3KB) per directory
- **8+ Maps of Content** covering major topic clusters
- **6+ wiki-links per note** on average

The `/vault-keeper` skill enforces these automatically.

---

## Key Entry Points

| Need | Start Here |
|------|------------|
| Agent architecture & multi-agent systems | `[[MOC-agentic-ai]]` |
| Quantum mechanics, computing, sensors | `[[MOC-quantum-physics]]` |
| Vault structure, linking, health | `[[MOC-vault-architecture]]` |
| MCP, SurrealDB, CI/CD, infrastructure | `[[MOC-platform-infrastructure]]` |
| ML, transformers, optimization | `[[MOC-machine-learning]]` |
| Space, JWST, cosmology | `[[MOC-astrophysics]]` |
| Compound sessions, retrospectives | `[[MOC-compound-engineering]]` |
| AI safety, alignment, guardrails | `[[MOC-safety-alignment]]` |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse hook: Proactive vault keeper checks on .md files.
#
# Two modes, same script:
#   Write/Edit → per-file checks + vault-wide pulse (60s cooldown)
#   Read       → vault-wide pulse only (5 min cooldown)
#
# Any agent touching vault .md files gets health awareness injected.
# Alerts are prefixed with VAULT_KEEPER: so the agent can detect and act on them.

VAULT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"

# ── Extract tool info from stdin JSON ─────────────────────────────────────────
stdin_json=$(cat)

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
fi

tool_name=$(echo "$stdin_json" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null)
file_path=$(echo "$stdin_json" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty' 2>/dev/null)

# Only run for .md files inside the vault
[[ -z "$file_path" ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" != *.md ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" != "$VAULT_ROOT"* ]] && exit 0

# Skip tooling directories
[[ "$file_path" == *"/obsidian-plugin/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/mcp-server/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/tools/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/.claude/"* ]] && exit 0

# ── Mode-specific cooldown ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$tool_name" == "Read" ]]; then
    COOLDOWN_FILE="/tmp/vault-keeper-read-$(id -u).last"
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS=300
else
    COOLDOWN_FILE="/tmp/vault-keeper-write-$(id -u).last"
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS=60
fi

if [[ -f "$COOLDOWN_FILE" ]]; then
    last_run=$(cat "$COOLDOWN_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
    now=$(date +%s)
    if [[ -n "$last_run" ]] && (( now - last_run < COOLDOWN_SECONDS )); then
        exit 0
    fi
fi

date +%s > "$COOLDOWN_FILE"

# ── Vault-wide checks (both Read and Write/Edit) ─────────────────────────────
alerts=""

# 1. Inbox
inbox_count=$(find "$VAULT_ROOT/inbox" -name '*.md' ! -name '.base' ! -name '_index.md' ! -name '_template.md' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
if [[ "$inbox_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: inbox has ${inbox_count} items waiting for triage\n"
fi

# ── Per-file checks (Write/Edit only) ────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$tool_name" != "Read" && -f "$file_path" ]]; then
    rel_path="${file_path#$VAULT_ROOT/}"
    dir_name="${rel_path%%/*}"

    # 2. Frontmatter
    first_line=$(head -1 "$file_path" 2>/dev/null)
    case "$dir_name" in
        concepts|papers|decisions|patterns|experiments|projects|lessons)
            if [[ "$first_line" != "---" ]]; then
                alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: note missing frontmatter — ${rel_path}\n"
            else
                tags_line=$(grep '^tags:' "$file_path" 2>/dev/null | head -1)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse hook: Proactive vault keeper checks on .md files.
#
# Two modes, same script:
#   Write/Edit → per-file checks + vault-wide pulse (60s cooldown)
#   Read       → vault-wide pulse only (5 min cooldown)
#
# Any agent touching vault .md files gets health awareness injected.
# Alerts are prefixed with VAULT_KEEPER: so the agent can detect and act on them.

VAULT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"

# ── Extract tool info from stdin JSON ─────────────────────────────────────────
stdin_json=$(cat)

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
fi

tool_name=$(echo "$stdin_json" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null)
file_path=$(echo "$stdin_json" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty' 2>/dev/null)

# Only run for .md files inside the vault
[[ -z "$file_path" ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" != *.md ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" != "$VAULT_ROOT"* ]] && exit 0

# Skip tooling directories
[[ "$file_path" == *"/obsidian-plugin/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/mcp-server/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/tools/"* ]] && exit 0
[[ "$file_path" == *"/.claude/"* ]] && exit 0

# ── Mode-specific cooldown ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$tool_name" == "Read" ]]; then
    COOLDOWN_FILE="/tmp/vault-keeper-read-$(id -u).last"
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS=300
else
    COOLDOWN_FILE="/tmp/vault-keeper-write-$(id -u).last"
    COOLDOWN_SECONDS=60
fi

if [[ -f "$COOLDOWN_FILE" ]]; then
    last_run=$(cat "$COOLDOWN_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
    now=$(date +%s)
    if [[ -n "$last_run" ]] && (( now - last_run < COOLDOWN_SECONDS )); then
        exit 0
    fi
fi

date +%s > "$COOLDOWN_FILE"

# ── Vault-wide checks (both Read and Write/Edit) ─────────────────────────────
alerts=""

# 1. Inbox
inbox_count=$(find "$VAULT_ROOT/inbox" -name '*.md' ! -name '.base' ! -name '_index.md' ! -name '_template.md' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
if [[ "$inbox_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: inbox has ${inbox_count} items waiting for triage\n"
fi

# ── Per-file checks (Write/Edit only) ────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$tool_name" != "Read" && -f "$file_path" ]]; then
    rel_path="${file_path#$VAULT_ROOT/}"
    dir_name="${rel_path%%/*}"

    # 2. Frontmatter
    first_line=$(head -1 "$file_path" 2>/dev/null)
    case "$dir_name" in
        concepts|papers|decisions|patterns|experiments|projects|lessons)
            if [[ "$first_line" != "---" ]]; then
                alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: note missing frontmatter — ${rel_path}\n"
            else
                tags_line=$(grep '^tags:' "$file_path" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
                if [[ -n "$tags_line" ]] && ! echo "$tags_line" | grep -q '\['; then
                    alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: note has tags as string (should be array) — ${rel_path}\n"
                fi
            fi
            ;;
    esac

    # 3. Inbound links
    basename_md="${file_path##*/}"
    name="${basename_md%.md}"
    if [[ "$name" != "_template" && "$name" != "_index" && "$name" != "MOC-"* ]]; then
        inbound=$(grep -rl "\[\[.*${name}" "$VAULT_ROOT/concepts/" "$VAULT_ROOT/papers/" "$VAULT_ROOT/decisions/" "$VAULT_ROOT/patterns/" "$VAULT_ROOT/projects/" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$file_path" | wc -l)
        if [[ "$inbound" -eq 0 ]]; then
            alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: new note has no inbound links — ${rel_path}\n"
        fi
    fi

    # 4. Canvas nudge — high link density suggests visual mapping
    outbound=$(grep -coh '\[\[[^]]*\]\]' "$file_path" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
    canvas_path="${file_path%.md}.canvas"
    if [[ "$outbound" -ge 10 && ! -f "$canvas_path" ]]; then
        alerts="${alerts}VAULT_KEEPER: note has ${outbound} outbound links — consider a companion .canvas to visualize relationships\n"
    fi
fi

# ── Output alerts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ -n "$alerts" ]]; then
    echo -e "$alerts"
fi

exit 0

Here's what changed and why it compounds:

### Three moves, same infrastructure

**1. `AGENTS.md`** — One file at vault root. OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, and 20+ tools read it at session start. Points them at `VAULT_MANIFEST.md` for the full map. Claude Code keeps reading `CLAUDE.md`. Zero conflict, universal reach.

**2. Rich Formats in VAULT_MANIFEST** — The manifest already teaches agents where to put notes. Now it also teaches *how* to make them rich:

| Format | Syntax | When |
|--------|--------|------|
| Callouts | `> [!tip]` | Decisions need consequences, lessons need the mistake |
| Mermaid | ` ```mermaid` | 3+ interacting components |
| Math | `$...$` | Quantitative papers, physics, ML |
| Aliases | `aliases: [...]` | Concepts with abbreviations or multiple names |
| Embeds | `![[note]]` | MOCs pulling in key sections |
| Heading links | `[[note#heading]]` | Precise cross-references |

Every agent reads this at session start. They learn the formats before they write their first note.

**3. Hook nudges** — Same `vault-keeper-check.sh`, three new checks:

| Check | Fires When | Nudge |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| Callouts | Decision/lesson/pattern with no `> [!` | "consider > [!warning] for consequences" |
| Aliases | Concept with no `aliases:` field | "consider adding aliases for discoverability" |
| Canvas | Note with 10+ outbound links, no `.canvas` | "consider a companion canvas" |

The hook that enforces health now also promotes richness. Same cooldown, same infrastructure, more dimensions.

Write a 500-word research-style framing of JourneyTracker and DegradationDetector as a *contribution to agent evaluation methodology*. This document doesn't exist anywhere in the vault. What exists are implementation notes and session references. What's needed is a statement legible to someone who evaluates research.

## Why This Matters

Evaluating whether an AI system is doing what you think it's doing is one of the hardest open problems in agentic AI — and it's central to Anthropic Universes work. JourneyTracker measures reasoning quality in trajectory space rather than action outcomes. DegradationDetector tracks when and how agent reasoning degrades. These are direct, concrete answers to that hard problem.

Right now this contribution is invisible because it's described in engineering terms, not research terms. A 500-word framing bridges that gap.

- **Motivation:** Why action-outcome metrics are insufficient for evaluating agent reasoning quality

- **Limitations:** What they don't measure, where they could be wrong (this is the part that signals research maturity)
- **Open questions:** What would need to be true for these to be rigorous

## What This Unlocks

This 500-word note becomes the core of the "evaluation methodology" section of the application. It also forces clarity about what claims can and can't be made — which is exactly the epistemic honesty Anthropic wants to see.

# Stop Assessing, Start Changing

**Triage target:** `lessons/` — this note is itself a lesson candidate

## Observation

The vault has been assessed four times in three days (2026-03-03 through 2026-03-05). Each assessment is sharp and accurate. None of them changed the graph metrics. Papers: 102. Concepts: 317. Links: 1,458. Delta across all four assessments: zero.

The compound engineering philosophy states that each session should leave the system more capable than it found it. Assessment sessions that produce only more assessment notes are not compounding — they are documenting the absence of compounding.

## The Pattern to Break

Assessment → insightful diagnosis → no implementation → next assessment references previous assessment → same diagnosis restated with additional nuance → still no implementation.

This pattern is not unique to this vault. It is a common failure mode in any system where planning is easier to execute than the work being planned. The vault infrastructure makes it especially easy: writing a note is frictionless, running a diagnostic is not.

## The Rule Going Forward

Before any new assessment note is written, at least one of the following must be true:
1. A concrete vault artifact was changed (not just read)
2. A diagnostic was run and its output is recorded
3. A dead wikilink was resolved to an actual note

If none of these is true, the session's output belongs in `inbox/` as a triage item, not in `projects/` as an assessment.

## What "Changed" Looks Like

- `concepts/flume-architecture.md` exists with actual content (not a stub)
- `experiments/2026-03-XX-flume-kl-validation.md` has real numbers
- `concepts/agentic-system-failure-taxonomy.md` groups the 45 lessons
- One of the 35 dead portfolio wikilinks resolves to a real note

These are the minimum viable outputs of a compounding session. Not plans to do them — the actual things.

# Run FLUME KL Collapse Diagnostic — This Week

Run the Phase 1 validation diagnostics identified in [[2026-02-23-flume-strategic-roadmap]]. Specifically: KL collapse check and reconstruction fidelity measurement. These were flagged as "start immediately" on 2026-02-23. It is now 2026-03-05 — ten days later — and they haven't run.

The entire April portfolio submission is built around FLUME. If KL collapse is present, or reconstruction fidelity is below ~70%, the narrative foundation is compromised. No amount of demo polish or asset generation fixes that. The validation *is* the portfolio work — it's not a prerequisite.

An Anthropic reviewer asking "have you checked for KL collapse?" needs a result, not a roadmap.

1. Plot KL loss trajectory across training epochs — is it annealing to a non-zero value, or collapsing to zero?

3. Sample 50 synthetic trajectories from the prior — are they coherent?
4. Log results as a vault experiment note with actual numbers

- KL healthy + reconstruction >70%: proceed to demo, asset generation, portfolio repo

- Reconstruction poor: architecture rework needed — this changes the timeline, better to know now

title: "FLUME KL Collapse Diagnostic"
date: 2026-03-05
status: proposed
tags: [experiment, flume, validation, machine-learning]
aliases: ["KL collapse check", "FLUME validation diagnostic"]
---

# FLUME KL Collapse Diagnostic

> [!danger] Urgency
> The entire April portfolio submission is built around FLUME. If KL collapse is present or reconstruction fidelity is below ~70%, the narrative foundation is compromised. No amount of demo polish fixes that. Ten days have passed since this was flagged as "start immediately" in [[2026-02-23-flume-strategic-roadmap]].

## Hypothesis

The FLUME variational autoencoder is training correctly — KL divergence is annealing to a non-zero value (not collapsing to zero), and the decoder can reconstruct semantically faithful trajectories from the latent space.

## Method

1. **KL loss trajectory** — Plot KL loss across training epochs. Healthy: anneals to a stable non-zero value. Collapsed: drops to zero (posterior = prior, latent space unused).
2. **Reconstruction fidelity** — Encode 50 real trajectories → decode → measure semantic preservation via token BLEU and entailment score. Target: >70%.
3. **Prior sampling coherence** — Sample 50 synthetic trajectories from the prior distribution. Evaluate whether decoded outputs are coherent agent trajectories or noise.
4. **Log results** — Record all numbers as a vault experiment note. No narrative without data.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Run KL diagnostic] --> B{KL healthy?}
    B -->|Yes| C{Reconstruction >70%?}
    B -->|No| D[Fix: β annealing / prior adjustment]
    C -->|Yes| E[Proceed to demo + portfolio]
    C -->|No| F[Architecture rework needed]
    D --> G[1-2 days, re-run diagnostic]
    F --> H[Timeline changes — escalate]
    E --> I[Asset generation + portfolio repo]
```

## Decision Points

> [!success] Green Path
> KL healthy + reconstruction >70% → proceed to demo, asset generation, portfolio repo.

> [!warning] Yellow Path
> KL collapse detected → fix with β annealing or prior adjustment. 1-2 day fix, not weeks. Re-run diagnostic.

> [!danger] Red Path
> Reconstruction poor despite healthy KL → architecture rework needed. This changes the timeline. Better to know now than at submission.

# FLUME KL Collapse Diagnostic

> [!danger] Urgency
> The entire April portfolio submission is built around FLUME. If KL collapse is present or reconstruction fidelity is below ~70%, the narrative foundation is compromised. No amount of demo polish fixes that. Ten days have passed since this was flagged as "start immediately" in [[2026-02-23-flume-strategic-roadmap]].

## Hypothesis

The FLUME variational autoencoder is training correctly — KL divergence is annealing to a non-zero value (not collapsing to zero), and the decoder can reconstruct semantically faithful trajectories from the latent space.

## Method

1. **KL loss trajectory** — Plot KL loss across training epochs. Healthy: anneals to a stable non-zero value. Collapsed: drops to zero (posterior = prior, latent space unused).
2. **Reconstruction fidelity** — Encode 50 real trajectories → decode → measure semantic preservation via token BLEU and entailment score. Target: >70%.
3. **Prior sampling coherence** — Sample 50 synthetic trajectories from the prior distribution. Evaluate whether decoded outputs are coherent agent trajectories or noise.
4. **Log results** — Record all numbers as a vault experiment note. No narrative without data.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Run KL diagnostic] --> B{KL healthy?}
    B -->|Yes| C{Reconstruction >70%?}
    B -->|No| D[Fix: β annealing / prior adjustment]
    C -->|Yes| E[Proceed to demo + portfolio]
    C -->|No| F[Architecture rework needed]
    D --> G[1-2 days, re-run diagnostic]
    F --> H[Timeline changes — escalate]
    E --> I[Asset generation + portfolio repo]
```

## Decision Points

> [!success] Green Path
> KL healthy + reconstruction >70% → proceed to demo, asset generation, portfolio repo.

> [!warning] Yellow Path
> KL collapse detected → fix with β annealing or prior adjustment. 1-2 day fix, not weeks. Re-run diagnostic.

> [!danger] Red Path
> Reconstruction poor despite healthy KL → architecture rework needed. This changes the timeline. Better to know now than at submission.

20-30 hours to run diagnostics and document results. This is the highest-information-per-hour task currently open.

# Agent Journey Tracking

Agent journey tracking is the practice of recording the full execution trace of an agent session — every task attempted, tool call made, decision taken, and output produced — so the session can be analyzed retrospectively and its learnings fed back into future sessions. In Cohezion, this is implemented through the `JourneyTracker` component, which records 12-dimensional position data representing the agent's location in the compound learning space.

Each execution step is logged as a state transition: the input, the action taken, the result, and the coherence score after the action. This trajectory data serves two purposes: real-time anomaly detection (identifying coherence collapse or drift mid-session) and post-session retrospection (extracting patterns and lessons for skill refinement). The [[non-blocking-observability]] pattern ensures tracking never blocks the primary execution path.

The 12D coordinate system maps agent state across multiple axes including task complexity, coherence, token efficiency, and skill coverage. Trajectory analysis of 5.5M simulated agent paths (from the [[universe-simulation]]) revealed the predictive throttling pattern — detecting velocity gradients in trajectory space to anticipate resource exhaustion before it occurs.

# Experience Feedback Loop

The experience feedback loop is the mechanism by which agent session outcomes — successes, failures, unexpected discoveries — are captured, structured, and injected back into future sessions to improve performance. It is the engine of [[compound-engineering]]: without a feedback loop, each session starts from scratch; with one, each session builds on all prior sessions.

The loop operates in four stages. First, a session executes and produces outputs (code, decisions, experiment results). Second, observations are saved to vault memory via `vault_push_memory` and `vault_push_session_state`. Third, structured lessons are extracted using `vault_log_decision` or `vault_log_experiment`, creating durable, searchable records. Fourth, future sessions load relevant prior context via `vault_find_relevant_context` and `vault_pull_session_context`, grounding new work in accumulated institutional knowledge.

The empirical payoff is substantial: [[lesson-37-experience-guided-execution-works-new]] demonstrated that experience-guided execution produces materially better outputs than cold-start sessions. Over 100 sessions, the feedback loop compounds to 7x+ token efficiency gains — not from doing the same work faster, but from not repeating mistakes and not rediscovering solutions that are already in the vault.

## Stages
1. **Execute**: Agent session runs, producing outputs and encountering decisions
2. **Capture**: Observations saved to vault memory; raw session state preserved
3. **Extract**: Lessons formalized via `vault_log_decision`, `vault_log_experiment`, `vault_extract_pattern`
4. **Inject**: Future sessions load relevant context via `vault_find_relevant_context`
5. **Improve**: Agents refine skills based on accumulated patterns; SkillRefiner updates PRIME definitions

## Related
- [[compound-engineering]] — the methodology the feedback loop implements
- [[meta-learning]] — the strategic layer that extracts patterns from the feedback loop
- [[agent-journey-tracking]] — the observability layer that records what happened during execution
- [[context-management]] — how prior experience is assembled and delivered to new sessions
- [[Ouroboros-Loop]] — the real-time autonomic Sense/Feel/Act cycle that operationalizes feedback during active sessions
- [[FLUME-Architecture]] -- FLUME embeddings close the feedback loop by making prior session knowledge retrievable for context injection

# Experience Feedback Loop

The experience feedback loop is the mechanism by which agent session outcomes — successes, failures, unexpected discoveries — are captured, structured, and injected back into future sessions to improve performance. It is the engine of [[compound-engineering]]: without a feedback loop, each session starts from scratch; with one, each session builds on all prior sessions.

The loop operates in four stages. First, a session executes and produces outputs (code, decisions, experiment results). Second, observations are saved to vault memory via `vault_push_memory` and `vault_push_session_state`. Third, structured lessons are extracted using `vault_log_decision` or `vault_log_experiment`, creating durable, searchable records. Fourth, future sessions load relevant prior context via `vault_find_relevant_context` and `vault_pull_session_context`, grounding new work in accumulated institutional knowledge.

The empirical payoff is substantial: [[lesson-37-experience-guided-execution-works-new]] demonstrated that experience-guided execution produces materially better outputs than cold-start sessions. Over 100 sessions, the feedback loop compounds to 7x+ token efficiency gains — not from doing the same work faster, but from not repeating mistakes and not rediscovering solutions that are already in the vault.

## Stages
1. **Execute**: Agent session runs, producing outputs and encountering decisions
2. **Capture**: Observations saved to vault memory; raw session state preserved
3. **Extract**: Lessons formalized via `vault_log_decision`, `vault_log_experiment`, `vault_extract_pattern`
4. **Inject**: Future sessions load relevant context via `vault_find_relevant_context`
5. **Improve**: Agents refine skills based on accumulated patterns; SkillRefiner updates PRIME definitions

# Agent Journey Tracking

Agent journey tracking is the practice of recording the full execution trace of an agent session — every task attempted, tool call made, decision taken, and output produced — so the session can be analyzed retrospectively and its learnings fed back into future sessions. In Cohezion, this is implemented through the `JourneyTracker` component, which records 12-dimensional position data representing the agent's location in the compound learning space.

Each execution step is logged as a state transition: the input, the action taken, the result, and the coherence score after the action. This trajectory data serves two purposes: real-time anomaly detection (identifying coherence collapse or drift mid-session) and post-session retrospection (extracting patterns and lessons for skill refinement). The [[non-blocking-observability]] pattern ensures tracking never blocks the primary execution path.

The 12D coordinate system maps agent state across multiple axes including task complexity, coherence, token efficiency, and skill coverage. Trajectory analysis of 5.5M simulated agent paths (from the [[universe-simulation]]) revealed the predictive throttling pattern — detecting velocity gradients in trajectory space to anticipate resource exhaustion before it occurs.

## Definition

**Compound engineering** is a knowledge management approach where decisions, experiments, and patterns are systematically captured and accumulated so they compound into reusable knowledge over time. Rather than treating each engineering session as isolated work, compound engineering treats every decision, failed experiment, and discovered pattern as an asset that makes future work faster and better-informed.

## How It Works

The approach rests on three pillars, each with a corresponding vault directory:

1. **Decisions** (`decisions/`) — Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) capture the *why* behind choices. When a similar question arises later, the prior reasoning is available — including the alternatives that were considered and rejected. See the [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor]] ADR for an example.

2. **Experiments** (`experiments/`) — Hypothesis-driven logs capture what was tried, what happened, and what was learned. Failed experiments are as valuable as successful ones — they prevent repeating dead ends. See [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes]] for an example.

3. **Patterns** (`patterns/`) — Reusable solutions extracted from project work. When a problem is solved well, the solution is generalized and stored for future use, including code examples and guidance on when to apply it.

## The Compounding Effect

The value of the vault grows nonlinearly:

- **Session 1** produces a few notes. The vault is a simple record.
- **Session 10** has enough prior decisions that new work starts by checking what was already decided. Redundant research is eliminated.
- **Session 100** has a rich web of cross-linked decisions, experiments, and patterns. New projects begin with relevant context automatically surfaced. The vault becomes an institutional memory that survives context windows, session boundaries, and team changes.

## Role in the Cohezion Vault

The Cohezion vault is built around compound engineering. The Cloud Vault MCP Server exposes this workflow programmatically through three operation layers:

- **`VaultOps`** — Core read/write/search operations on the vault filesystem
- **`CompoundOps`** — Structured logging of decisions, experiments, and patterns with enforced frontmatter schemas
- **`ObsidianOps`** — Cross-linking via backlinks, tags, and wiki-links that connect knowledge across directories

The `inbox/` directory serves as the entry point: raw ideas are captured quickly, then processed into the appropriate permanent directory. The proposed [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor|inbox processor daemon]] would automate this flow, using AI to classify and structure incoming notes.

## Relationship to AI-Assisted Engineering

Compound engineering is especially powerful when combined with AI agents:

- Agents can **read** prior decisions and patterns before starting new work, avoiding known pitfalls
- Agents can **write** structured records of their own decisions and discoveries, contributing to the vault
- The vault provides **persistent memory** that spans across context windows and sessions — solving the "blank slate" problem where each AI conversation starts from zero

The [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes|research agent experiment]] demonstrated that AI agents can autonomously produce vault-quality content, validating the compound engineering workflow end-to-end.

# AI Safety

AI safety is the research and engineering field dedicated to ensuring that AI systems behave safely and beneficially, especially as they become more capable and autonomous. It encompasses four major subfields: alignment (systems pursue intended goals), interpretability (humans can understand system reasoning), robustness (systems fail gracefully under distributional shift), and governance (institutional structures for responsible deployment).

For agentic AI systems, safety concerns are especially acute because agents act in the world rather than merely generating text. An agent with access to file systems, APIs, and external services can cause irreversible harm if misaligned. The primary safety mechanisms are: constrained tool permissions (agents can only access what they need), action auditing (every tool call is logged), reversibility preference (prefer reversible actions over irreversible ones), and human oversight checkpoints (mandatory approval before irreversible actions).

Cohezion addresses AI safety through its CONSTITUTION.md (hard constraints no agent may violate), the VaultExecutionLogger (immutable audit trail), and the practice of [[adversarial-review]] before execution. The GuardrailPipeline performs input/output safety checks on agent decisions. The [[lesson-26-never-print-credentials]] lesson captures the most critical operational safety rule: secrets must never appear in logs.

# Shoshin Assessment — Beginner's Mind Reading of the Vault

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6), 2026-03-05. Beginner's mind — no prior context loaded.*

---

## The Core Observation

The vault has developed a sophisticated internal language that is increasingly self-referential. Concepts link to concepts that link back to the first concept. The system has learned to mistake describing work for doing work. This is exactly the failure mode compound engineering was designed to prevent.

---

## What Is Actually Here

- 102 papers, 317 concepts, 1,458 links
- 45 hard-won operational lessons from real failures
- An N-body simulation that generated 5.5M real trajectories overnight
- A VAE architecture (FLUME) with a real encoder/decoder design
- A multi-agent council capable of structured democratic deliberation
- A lessons corpus that constitutes a genuine failure taxonomy

---

## What Is Described as Being Here But Isn't

- Any FLUME validation results (KL collapse status unknown, reconstruction fidelity unmeasured)
- A portfolio repository
- 35 portfolio assets
- An end-to-end working demo
- A Platform Spine — canonical notes describing what the platform *is*
- A research narrative legible to someone outside the system

---

## The Self-Reference Problem

The `compound-engineering.md` concept note lists 8 implementation plans, 12 roadmaps, 16 versions of strategic documents, 4 "desperation mode" variants, and a readiness report. The `cohezion.md` note's agent outputs include a business plan, a tax strategy report, and a manifesto. The `anthropic-research-engineer.md` note's substantive content is mostly a list of cover letter and resume versions.

The night council voted 8-2 on narrative architecture and produced a second-by-second demo script. It has never run a single FLUME diagnostic.

This is the pattern: sophisticated planning infrastructure producing more planning infrastructure.

---

## The Internal Language Problem

The vault has accumulated terminology — HIHO_STABILITY_PRIME, TEMPORAL_PRECISION_PRIME, REALITY_PRECIPITATION_PRIME, void-to-swarm precipitation, toroidal singularity — that is evocative but opaque. A beginner reading `universe-simulation.md` cannot determine what these compute. An Anthropic reviewer will encounter the same opacity.

Compound engineering philosophy: knowledge should be retrievable and usable by a cold session. Much of the vault's most important content is not — it requires initiation into a private vocabulary before it can be understood.

---

## What a Beginner Would Do

1. Write one paragraph about what FLUME does that a physicist could understand without knowing what "12D compound engineering space" means
2. Run the KL diagnostic — stop planning to run it
3. Write the 45-lesson taxonomy — the lessons are real, the taxonomy is not
4. Delete or archive half the concept stubs — thin nodes with only internal links are noise, not knowledge
5. Stop naming things with PRIME suffixes — show what they compute instead

---

## The Genuine Assets Worth Protecting

These are real and impressive. They should be the center of the portfolio, not buried under meta-commentary:

- **The 45-lesson corpus** — empirical taxonomy of agentic system failure modes; publishable
- **The 5.5M trajectory simulation** — real overnight data from a real physics engine
- **JourneyTracker and DegradationDetector** — direct answers to the hardest problem in agent evaluation
- **The night council's constraint discipline** — read-only scoping, deferred financial commitments, democratic rationale logging; this is working aligned multi-agent AI
- **The FLUME architecture** — if validated, genuinely novel; if not validated, still demonstrates the right instinct

---

## The Honest Summary

The vault is not broken. But it has drifted. The compounding is happening at the layer of documentation and planning, not at the layer of knowledge and results. The ratio of "notes describing future work" to "notes containing results of completed work" is badly skewed.

A first-time reader — a beginner — would find the genuine contributions buried under layers of roadmaps, strategic frameworks, narrative architectures, and agent output logs. That is the problem to fix before April.

The vault doesn't need more assessment. It needs the center of gravity to shift from planning to showing.

---

## Related

- [[stop-assessing-start-changing]]
- [[lesson-measurement-integrity-honest-reporting]]
- [[FLUME-Architecture]]
- [[2026-03-04-vault-assessment-v3]]
- [[lessons-corpus-taxonomy]]
- [[flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic]]

---
title: "Compound Engineering"
date: "2026-02-07"
tags: [concept, methodology, knowledge-management]
---

## Definition

**Compound engineering** is a knowledge management approach where decisions, experiments, and patterns are systematically captured and accumulated so they compound into reusable knowledge over time. Rather than treating each engineering session as isolated work, compound engineering treats every decision, failed experiment, and discovered pattern as an asset that makes future work faster and better-informed.

## How It Works

The approach rests on three pillars, each with a corresponding vault directory:

1. **Decisions** (`decisions/`) — Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) capture the *why* behind choices. When a similar question arises later, the prior reasoning is available — including the alternatives that were considered and rejected. See the [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor]] ADR for an example.

2. **Experiments** (`experiments/`) — Hypothesis-driven logs capture what was tried, what happened, and what was learned. Failed experiments are as valuable as successful ones — they prevent repeating dead ends. See [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes]] for an example.

3. **Patterns** (`patterns/`) — Reusable solutions extracted from project work. When a problem is solved well, the solution is generalized and stored for future use, including code examples and guidance on when to apply it.

## The Compounding Effect

The value of the vault grows nonlinearly:

- **Session 1** produces a few notes. The vault is a simple record.
- **Session 10** has enough prior decisions that new work starts by checking what was already decided. Redundant research is eliminated.
- **Session 100** has a rich web of cross-linked decisions, experiments, and patterns. New projects begin with relevant context automatically surfaced. The vault becomes an institutional memory that survives context windows, session boundaries, and team changes.

## Role in the Cohezion Vault

The Cohezion vault is built around compound engineering. The Cloud Vault MCP Server exposes this workflow programmatically through three operation layers:

- **`VaultOps`** — Core read/write/search operations on the vault filesystem
- **`CompoundOps`** — Structured logging of decisions, experiments, and patterns with enforced frontmatter schemas
- **`ObsidianOps`** — Cross-linking via backlinks, tags, and wiki-links that connect knowledge across directories

The `inbox/` directory serves as the entry point: raw ideas are captured quickly, then processed into the appropriate permanent directory. The proposed [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor|inbox processor daemon]] would automate this flow, using AI to classify and structure incoming notes.

## Relationship to AI-Assisted Engineering

Compound engineering is especially powerful when combined with AI agents:

- Agents can **read** prior decisions and patterns before starting new work, avoiding known pitfalls
- Agents can **write** structured records of their own decisions and discoveries, contributing to the vault
- The vault provides **persistent memory** that spans across context windows and sessions — solving the "blank slate" problem where each AI conversation starts from zero

The [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes|research agent experiment]] demonstrated that AI agents can autonomously produce vault-quality content, validating the compound engineering workflow end-to-end.

## Primary Sources

- Andrew S. Grove (1983). *High Output Management*. [https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884](https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884) — Grove's principle that strategic decisions made early disproportionately affect organizational leverage; early planning pays off 10x
- Communications of the ACM (2024). *Knowledge Management with Patterns*. [https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/](https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/)
- Lifecycle Insights (2024). *Engineering Knowledge Management*. [https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management](https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management)

## Core Principles

1. **Validate Before Scaling**: [[implementation-first-infrastructure-later]] — Prove concepts with minimal tokens before investing in infrastructure

3. **Template Reuse**: [[template-reuse]] — Copy working patterns (87% token savings) instead of building from scratch
4. **Meta-Learning**: [[meta-learning]] — Extract lessons from failures (7.6x → 757x ROI over 100 projects)
5. **ROI Analysis**: [[roi-analysis]] — Measure compound returns to prioritize high-reuse investments
6. **Structured Capture**: Use CompoundOps to enforce frontmatter schemas for decisions/experiments/patterns

# Vault Insight — The Two Cohezions

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6), 2026-03-05. Based on reading the full vault including missions/anthropic-portfolio/.*

---

## The Discovery

Reading across the full vault reveals something the previous assessments missed: there are two distinct versions of Cohezion living in the same vault, and they are in tension with each other.

**Cohezion A** — the one in `experiments/`, `lessons/`, `concepts/compound-engineering.md`, the HANDOFF, the session notes — is a real, rigorous, empirically-grounded platform. It has 45 hard-won lessons from actual failures. It has a VAE training run with real numbers (KL divergence 4.2 nats, 53% reconstruction improvement, t-SNE clusters corresponding to session outcomes). It has an N-body simulation that ran overnight and produced 5.5M trajectories. It has a branching strategy problem it is honestly trying to solve. It has technical debt it has explicitly named.

**Cohezion B** — the one in `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md`, the CONSTITUTION's "0.5 Coherence Rule," the CHARTER's "HIHO Stability," the references to "The Awareness of Nothing at All," "void-to-swarm precipitation," "S8 Tension Resolution," "Neutrino-Dark Matter Coupling (ν_dm = 0.03)" — is a different thing entirely. It invokes Bob Greenyer's FTM research, Wilbert Smith's Tensor Beam, Ken Shoulders' EVO, and Takaaki Matsumoto's ENC as a "Source Code for Reality." It calls the portfolio "unignorable" and recommends submitting immediately.

These two Cohezions are not reconcilable. One is a research engineering platform that Anthropic would take seriously. The other would cause an Anthropic hiring manager to close the tab.

---

## The Adversarial Review Missed the Real Problem

The `ADVERSARIAL_PORTFOLIO_REVIEW_20260225.md` is formally structured and caught one real issue — the VAE fallback to hash encoding. But its conclusion ("Submit immediately. This is unignorable.") is the wrong answer to the wrong question. The review verified internal consistency. It did not ask the prior question: *does this framing make sense to an external reader who doesn't share the conceptual vocabulary?*

The README opens with:

> *"The Awareness of Nothing precipitates the Tensor Beam across the 4 Fabrics, manifesting the Fractal Toroidal EVO—governed by the S8 Tension Resolution and the 100x Peaked Manifold Approximation."*

This is the first thing an Anthropic reviewer would read. No amount of verified Maxwell equations or confirmed 424x VLIW speedup recovers from that opening.

---

## Why This Happened

The vault's internal language evolved in a closed loop. Each session built on the vocabulary of the prior session. "HIHO Stability" became a defined term. "Reality precipitation" became a technical concept. "The Quantum Nano-Banana" became a named artifact. The adversarial review validated claims *within* this vocabulary without stepping outside it.

This is a real risk of compound engineering: the vocabulary compounds along with the knowledge, and eventually the vocabulary becomes a barrier rather than a bridge. What started as evocative shorthand became load-bearing terminology that cannot be understood without reading weeks of session history.

---

## What Is Actually Strong in the Portfolio

Buried under Cohezion B, the genuine Cohezion A contributions are compelling:

- **VLIW 424x speedup** — verified, ILP-driven, single-core constrained. This is real and impressive.

> These are the whole story. Not a footnote to a cosmological framework.

- Night council asset generation redirected to Cohezion A framing
- Internal vocabulary remains available for sessions but excluded from external materials
- All external content passes the "cold reader" test

---
title: "Compound Engineering"
date: "2026-02-07"
tags: [concept, methodology, knowledge-management]
---

## Definition

**Compound engineering** is a knowledge management approach where decisions, experiments, and patterns are systematically captured and accumulated so they compound into reusable knowledge over time. Rather than treating each engineering session as isolated work, compound engineering treats every decision, failed experiment, and discovered pattern as an asset that makes future work faster and better-informed.

## How It Works

The approach rests on three pillars, each with a corresponding vault directory:

1. **Decisions** (`decisions/`) — Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) capture the *why* behind choices. When a similar question arises later, the prior reasoning is available — including the alternatives that were considered and rejected. See the [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor]] ADR for an example.

2. **Experiments** (`experiments/`) — Hypothesis-driven logs capture what was tried, what happened, and what was learned. Failed experiments are as valuable as successful ones — they prevent repeating dead ends. See [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes]] for an example.

3. **Patterns** (`patterns/`) — Reusable solutions extracted from project work. When a problem is solved well, the solution is generalized and stored for future use, including code examples and guidance on when to apply it.

## The Compounding Effect

The value of the vault grows nonlinearly:

- **Session 1** produces a few notes. The vault is a simple record.
- **Session 10** has enough prior decisions that new work starts by checking what was already decided. Redundant research is eliminated.
- **Session 100** has a rich web of cross-linked decisions, experiments, and patterns. New projects begin with relevant context automatically surfaced. The vault becomes an institutional memory that survives context windows, session boundaries, and team changes.

## Role in the Cohezion Vault

The Cohezion vault is built around compound engineering. The Cloud Vault MCP Server exposes this workflow programmatically through three operation layers:

- **`VaultOps`** — Core read/write/search operations on the vault filesystem
- **`CompoundOps`** — Structured logging of decisions, experiments, and patterns with enforced frontmatter schemas
- **`ObsidianOps`** — Cross-linking via backlinks, tags, and wiki-links that connect knowledge across directories

The `inbox/` directory serves as the entry point: raw ideas are captured quickly, then processed into the appropriate permanent directory. The proposed [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor|inbox processor daemon]] would automate this flow, using AI to classify and structure incoming notes.

## Relationship to AI-Assisted Engineering

Compound engineering is especially powerful when combined with AI agents:

- Agents can **read** prior decisions and patterns before starting new work, avoiding known pitfalls
- Agents can **write** structured records of their own decisions and discoveries, contributing to the vault
- The vault provides **persistent memory** that spans across context windows and sessions — solving the "blank slate" problem where each AI conversation starts from zero

The [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes|research agent experiment]] demonstrated that AI agents can autonomously produce vault-quality content, validating the compound engineering workflow end-to-end.

## Primary Sources

- Andrew S. Grove (1983). *High Output Management*. [https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884](https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884) — Grove's principle that strategic decisions made early disproportionately affect organizational leverage; early planning pays off 10x
- Communications of the ACM (2024). *Knowledge Management with Patterns*. [https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/](https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/)
- Lifecycle Insights (2024). *Engineering Knowledge Management*. [https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management](https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management)

## Core Principles

1. **Validate Before Scaling**: [[implementation-first-infrastructure-later]] — Prove concepts with minimal tokens before investing in infrastructure
2. **Token Efficiency**: [[token-efficiency]] — Optimize LLM token consumption to maximize output per token spent
3. **Template Reuse**: [[template-reuse]] — Copy working patterns (87% token savings) instead of building from scratch
4. **Meta-Learning**: [[meta-learning]] — Extract lessons from failures (7.6x → 757x ROI over 100 projects)
5. **ROI Analysis**: [[roi-analysis]] — Measure compound returns to prioritize high-reuse investments
6. **Structured Capture**: Use CompoundOps to enforce frontmatter schemas for decisions/experiments/patterns

# Adversarial Review

Adversarial review is the structured practice of critiquing a plan or design by assuming the proposer is wrong and generating falsifiable counter-hypotheses. Unlike standard review (which looks for obvious errors), adversarial review actively tries to invalidate the proposal — finding hidden assumptions, edge cases, and alternative explanations that the proposer's perspective is blind to.

The economic case for adversarial review is compelling: a 10-minute review investment (5K tokens) can prevent 8+ hours of wasted execution (225K+ tokens) when it catches a fundamental flaw before work begins. The ROI is 45x on a single catch. The [[lesson-adversarial-review-before-execution]] lesson, validated across multiple Cohezion sessions, established adversarial review as a mandatory gate before any significant implementation begins.

In Cohezion's spec workflow, adversarial review is institutionalized through the `plan-challenger` agent: a sub-agent that receives the completed plan and is explicitly instructed to challenge its assumptions, identify risks, and require evidence for key claims. This is the final quality gate before plan approval — the plan-challenger runs in parallel with the plan-verifier, and both must clear before implementation begins.

## Key Properties
- **Assumption inversion**: Assumes the proposer is wrong; requires positive evidence, not absence of objections
- **Counter-hypothesis generation**: Produces specific falsifiable alternative explanations
- **Evidence requirement**: Intuition alone is insufficient; claims must be backed by observable evidence
- **Mandatory gating**: Adversarial review is a blocking gate, not advisory feedback
- **Asymmetric value**: High catch rate on low-probability catastrophic failures justifies fixed review overhead

The user is asking about how the vault can communicate back to the platform and SurrealDB 3.0. This is about the MCP integration layer — making the vault not just a passive knowledge store but an active participant that pushes changes back to the platform infrastructure.

Let me understand what exists:
1. Cloud Vault MCP server on port 8360 — programmatic vault access
2. SurrealDB — stores the knowledge graph
3. The vault-keeper hooks — fire on Read/Write/Edit of .md files

The compound engineering insight: the hooks already fire on every vault change. They could push changes to SurrealDB, keeping the graph database in sync with the vault automatically. And SurrealDB 3.0 has new features worth investigating.


Now I need to dig into what SurrealDB 3.0 brings to the table, see how the current MCP and SurrealDB integration is wired up in this codebase, and figure out how to extend the hooks to actually push those changes back.

   602→    def start_watching(self) -> None:
   603→        """Start watching vault for file changes (real-time sync)."""
   604→        if self.observer is not None:
   605→            logger.warning("File watcher already running")
   606→            return
   607→
   608→        event_handler = VaultFileHandler(self)
   609→        self.observer = Observer()
   610→
   611→        # Watch papers and concepts directories
   612→        for subdir in ["papers", "concepts", "patterns", "decisions"]:
   613→            watch_path = self.vault_path / subdir
   614→            if watch_path.exists():
   615→                self.observer.schedule(event_handler, str(watch_path), recursive=False)
   616→                logger.info(f"Watching: {watch_path}")
   617→
   618→        self.observer.start()
   619→        logger.info("File watcher started")
   620→
   621→    def stop_watching(self) -> None:
   622→        """Stop watching vault for file changes."""
   623→        if self.observer is not None:
   624→            self.observer.stop()
   625→            self.observer.join()
   626→            self.observer = None
   627→            logger.info("File watcher stopped")
   628→
   629→    def close(self) -> None:
   630→        """Clean up resources."""
   631→        self.stop_watching()
   632→        self.client.close()
   633→        if self.async_client is not None:
   634→            asyncio.run(self.async_client.aclose())
   635→
   636→
   637→class VaultFileHandler(FileSystemEventHandler):
   638→    """Watchdog event handler for vault file changes."""
   639→
   640→    def __init__(self, sync: SurrealDBSync):
   641→        self.sync = sync
   642→
   643→    def on_modified(self, event: FileSystemEvent) -> None:
   644→        """Handle file modification events."""
   645→        if event.is_directory or not event.src_path.endswith(".md"):
   646→            return
   647→
   648→        path = Path(event.src_path)
   649→
   650→        # Determine file type and sync
   651→        if "papers" in path.parts:
   652→            self.sync.sync_paper(path)
   653→        elif "concepts" in path.parts:
   654→            self.sync.sync_concept(path)
   655→
   656→    def on_created(self, event: FileSystemEvent) -> None:
   657→        """Handle file creation events."""
   658→        self.on_modified(event)  # Same logic as modification
