| `papers/` | Research papers, articles, external sources | Summarizing external research with citations | `kebab-case-descriptive-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) | Recording a choice with context, alternatives, consequences | `YYYY-MM-DD-decision-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns | Documenting a repeatable solution to a recurring problem | `kebab-case-pattern-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results | Testing a hypothesis with method, results, learnings | `YYYY-MM-DD-experiment-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `projects/` | Project-level tracking and plans | Tracking a multi-session effort with goals and status | `YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `lessons/` | Lessons learned from mistakes/discoveries | Capturing something learned the hard way — prevents repeat mistakes | `kebab-case-lesson-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]`, `severity` |

### Workflow Directories (where work happens)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — triage point | Dropping raw ideas, unprocessed content, or agent output that needs classification | Any `.md` name |
| `daily/` | Daily notes, session logs, checkpoints | Recording a session's work, daily standup, or checkpoint | `YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` |
| `sessions/` | Formal session records with structured metadata | Documenting a compound engineering session with metrics | `session-NNN-*.md` |
| `missions/` | Multi-agent coordinated tasks | Orchestrating multiple agents toward a shared goal | `mission-name.md` or dated |
| `retrospectives/` | Post-session analysis | Reviewing what worked, what didn't, and why | `YYYY-MM-DD-retrospective.md` |
| `Agents/` | Agent execution records and walkthroughs | Storing agent run artifacts, traces, walkthroughs | `AgentName/UUID/` subdirs |

### Navigation Directories (how to find things)

| Directory | Purpose | Key Files |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `concepts/MOC-*.md` | Maps of Content — curated topic indexes | 8 MOCs: agentic-ai, quantum-physics, vault-architecture, platform-infrastructure, machine-learning, astrophysics, compound-engineering, safety-alignment |

### Infrastructure Directories (tooling, not content)

| Directory | Purpose | Agent Action |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases (no companion note) | Create spatial maps, architecture diagrams |
| `teleport/` | Cloud-to-local file sync (tasks + results) | Use for cross-environment transfers |
| `docs/` | Long-form documentation, brand guides | Reference only — don't create here without asking |
| `meta/` | Self-recording, compound demos | Specialized — check before writing |
| `specs/` | Formal specifications | For major system designs |
| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

---

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/
I mapped relationships visually        → companion .canvas next to the .md, or canvas/ if standalone
I don't know where this goes          → inbox/     (always safe default)
```

# Vault Manifest

**Read this first.** This file tells you where everything lives, where to put your output, and what conventions to follow.

## Directory Map

### Content Directories (where knowledge lives)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming | Required Frontmatter |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|---------------------|
| `concepts/` | Core definitions, frameworks, techniques | Defining a reusable idea, technology, or methodology | `kebab-case.md` (no date prefix) | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `papers/` | Research papers, articles, external sources | Summarizing external research with citations | `kebab-case-descriptive-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) | Recording a choice with context, alternatives, consequences | `YYYY-MM-DD-decision-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns | Documenting a repeatable solution to a recurring problem | `kebab-case-pattern-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results | Testing a hypothesis with method, results, learnings | `YYYY-MM-DD-experiment-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `projects/` | Project-level tracking and plans | Tracking a multi-session effort with goals and status | `YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `lessons/` | Lessons learned from mistakes/discoveries | Capturing something learned the hard way — prevents repeat mistakes | `kebab-case-lesson-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]`, `severity` |

### Workflow Directories (where work happens)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — triage point | Dropping raw ideas, unprocessed content, or agent output that needs classification | Any `.md` name |
| `daily/` | Daily notes, session logs, checkpoints | Recording a session's work, daily standup, or checkpoint | `YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` |
| `sessions/` | Formal session records with structured metadata | Documenting a compound engineering session with metrics | `session-NNN-*.md` |
| `missions/` | Multi-agent coordinated tasks | Orchestrating multiple agents toward a shared goal | `mission-name.md` or dated |
| `retrospectives/` | Post-session analysis | Reviewing what worked, what didn't, and why | `YYYY-MM-DD-retrospective.md` |
| `Agents/` | Agent execution records and walkthroughs | Storing agent run artifacts, traces, walkthroughs | `AgentName/UUID/` subdirs |

### Navigation Directories (how to find things)

| Directory | Purpose | Key Files |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `concepts/MOC-*.md` | Maps of Content — curated topic indexes | 8 MOCs: agentic-ai, quantum-physics, vault-architecture, platform-infrastructure, machine-learning, astrophysics, compound-engineering, safety-alignment |

### Infrastructure Directories (tooling, not content)

| Directory | Purpose | Agent Action |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases (no companion note) | Create spatial maps, architecture diagrams |
| `teleport/` | Cloud-to-local file sync (tasks + results) | Use for cross-environment transfers |
| `docs/` | Long-form documentation, brand guides | Reference only — don't create here without asking |
| `meta/` | Self-recording, compound demos | Specialized — check before writing |
| `specs/` | Formal specifications | For major system designs |
| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

---

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/
I mapped relationships visually        → companion .canvas next to the .md, or canvas/ if standalone
I don't know where this goes          → inbox/     (always safe default)
```

**When in doubt, use `inbox/`.** The vault keeper triages inbox items into their proper location with correct frontmatter and cross-links.

---

## Canvas Files (Multimodal Assets)

**Notes explain. Canvases show.** When a topic has complex relationships, spatial layout reveals structure that prose cannot. Create `.canvas` files alongside their companion `.md` notes.

### When to Create a Canvas

| Signal | Canvas Type |
|--------|-------------|
| MOC with 10+ linked notes | **Relationship map** — nodes for notes, edges for connections |
| Architecture or system design | **Architecture diagram** — groups for layers, text cards for components |
| Decision with 3+ alternatives | **Decision landscape** — cards per option, edges to trade-offs |
| Research cluster spanning domains | **Domain map** — grouped by field, edges for cross-domain links |
| Vault keeper nudges you | The hook detected 10+ outbound links — the note wants a canvas |

### Naming and Placement

Canvas files live **alongside their companion note**:
- `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.md` → `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.canvas`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.md` → `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.canvas`
- Standalone canvases (no companion note) → `canvas/` directory

### JSON Format

Obsidian canvas files are JSON with `nodes` and `edges`:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"unique-id", "type":"file", "file":"concepts/machine-learning.md", "x":0, "y":0, "width":250, "height":60},
    {"id":"label-1",   "type":"text", "text":"## Key Insight\n\nMarkdown content here", "x":300, "y":0, "width":300, "height":120, "color":"4"},
    {"id":"group-1",   "type":"group","label":"ML Cluster", "x":-50, "y":-50, "width":600, "height":250, "color":"2"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id":"edge-1", "fromNode":"unique-id", "toNode":"label-1", "label":"informs"}
  ]
}
```

**Node types:**
- `file` — link to a vault note (opens on click). Use `"file": "path/to/note.md"`
- `text` — inline markdown card. Use `"text": "## Title\n\nContent"`
- `group` — visual grouping box. Use `"label": "Group Name"`

**Colors:** `"1"` red, `"2"` orange, `"3"` yellow, `"4"` green, `"5"` cyan, `"6"` purple, or hex `"#RRGGGG"`

**Layout tips:** Use x/y grid spacing of ~300px horizontal, ~150px vertical. Groups should surround their children with ~50px padding.

> [!warning] Consequences

> [!danger] Known Failure

> [!example] Usage
> ```python

> ```

> [!abstract] Summary
> Three-sentence TL;DR of this paper or decision.

Make any paragraph linkable by adding `^block-id` at the end.

```markdown
The key insight is that context quality matters more than quantity. ^key-insight
```

Then reference from anywhere: `[[context-management#^key-insight]]`

---

## Conventions

### Frontmatter (YAML)

Every note in a content directory MUST have frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: "Note Title"
date: 2026-03-04
tags: [tag1, tag2, tag3]
aliases: ["alt name", "abbreviation"]
---
```

**Tags are ALWAYS arrays** — never comma-separated strings.
**Aliases are optional but encouraged** on concepts with multiple names or abbreviations.

**Status values by directory:**
- `decisions/`: `proposed` → `accepted` → `deprecated` | `rejected`
- `experiments/`: `in-progress` → `complete` | `failed`
- `projects/`: `active` → `complete` → `archived`

### Cross-References

Use Obsidian wiki-links: `[[note-name]]`

- Use bare filename (no path prefix): `[[machine-learning]]` not `[[concepts/machine-learning]]`
- Link at first mention of a concept
- Every note should have 3+ outbound wiki-links
- Every new note must be linked FROM at least one existing note (no orphans)

### Templates

Directories with `_template.md` files: `decisions/`, `patterns/`, `experiments/`, `projects/`, `daily/`

Copy the template when creating a new note in these directories.

---

## Quick Start for Agents

### Starting a session:
1. Read this manifest (you're doing it now)
2. Check `inbox/` for items needing triage
3. Load the relevant MOC for your task: `concepts/MOC-*.md`
4. Check `lessons/` for past mistakes related to your task

### During your session:
5. Create notes in the correct directory per routing rules above
6. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to connect every new note to 1-3 existing notes
7. Use proper frontmatter with tags as arrays

### Ending a session:
8. Log session summary to `daily/YYYY-MM-DD-session-id.md`
9. If you discovered something reusable, add it to `lessons/` or `patterns/`
10. Any raw output that needs triage → `inbox/`

---

## Vault Health Invariants

A healthy vault maintains:
- **0 orphan notes** in content directories
- **0 frontmatter issues** (missing or malformed)
- **0 broken wiki-links** (pointing to non-existent notes)
- **< 10% thin notes** (under 3KB) per directory
- **8+ Maps of Content** covering major topic clusters
- **6+ wiki-links per note** on average

The `/vault-keeper` skill enforces these automatically.

# Cohezion Vault

Knowledge base for the Cohezion agentic AI framework. Obsidian vault with 1,400+ notes, 11,000+ wiki-links, and 8 Maps of Content.

## Quick Orientation

**Read `VAULT_MANIFEST.md` first.** It maps every directory, explains output routing, and lists conventions. Each directory also has a `_index.md` with purpose, naming rules, and key notes.

## Structure

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `concepts/` | Core definitions, frameworks, techniques |
| `papers/` | Research papers and external sources |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns |
| `lessons/` | Hard-won knowledge from mistakes |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results |
| `projects/` | Multi-session project tracking |
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — safe default for any output |
| `daily/` | Session logs and daily notes |
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases |

## Conventions

- **Frontmatter:** YAML with `title`, `date`, `tags` (always arrays: `[tag1, tag2]`)
- **Cross-references:** Obsidian wiki-links `[[note-name]]` — bare filename, no path prefix
- **Rich formats encouraged:** Mermaid diagrams, callouts (`> [!tip]`), LaTeX math, `.canvas` files
- **Templates:** `_template.md` in each content directory — copy when creating notes

## Output Routing

```
Research summaries       → papers/
Techniques/definitions   → concepts/
Architectural choices    → decisions/
Reusable solutions       → patterns/
Mistakes and learnings   → lessons/
Visual relationship maps → companion .canvas alongside .md, or canvas/
Don't know where it goes → inbox/
```

## Entry Points (Maps of Content)

| Topic | MOC |
|-------|-----|
| Agent architecture | `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.md` |
| Quantum physics | `concepts/MOC-quantum-physics.md` |
| Vault structure | `concepts/MOC-vault-architecture.md` |
| Infrastructure | `concepts/MOC-platform-infrastructure.md` |
| Machine learning | `concepts/MOC-machine-learning.md` |
| Astrophysics | `concepts/MOC-astrophysics.md` |
| Methodology | `concepts/MOC-compound-engineering.md` |
| AI safety | `concepts/MOC-safety-alignment.md` |

## Build Commands (Tooling)

```bash
# Cohezion Engine CLI
cd tools/cohezion-engine && uv pip install -e .
cz --help

# 3D Graph Plugin
cd obsidian-plugin/3d-graph-plugin && npm install && npm run dev

# MCP Server
cd mcp-server && pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest
```

## MCP Integration

- **Cloud Vault MCP** on port 8360 — programmatic vault access (VaultOps, CompoundOps, ObsidianOps, SurrealDB)
- **Ollama MCP** on port 22360 — semantic search and embeddings

## Vault Health

The vault maintains these invariants automatically:
- 0 orphan notes, 0 frontmatter issues, 0 broken links
- 8+ Maps of Content, 6+ avg wiki-links per note
- Proactive hooks detect and alert on violations

## See Also

- `VAULT_MANIFEST.md` — full directory map, rich format specs, agent workflow
- `CLAUDE.md` — Claude Code-specific instructions and tool conventions

---
title: "Surrealdb"
date: 2026-02-19
tags: [concept, graph-databases, knowledge-graph-systems, agent-context]
related_concepts: [graphrag-knowledge-graph-with-surrealdb, knowledge-graph-systems, cloud-vault-mcp, agent-context, semantic-search]
---
## Definition

SurrealDB is a multi-model database that combines graph database capabilities, document storage, relational queries, and vector fields in a single system accessed through SurrealQL — a SQL-inspired query language with graph-native extensions. Unlike traditional databases that force a choice between document, relational, or graph models, SurrealDB handles all three simultaneously, making it well-suited for agent context graphs that need structured schema, relationship traversal, and vector similarity search.

SurrealDB's key differentiator for agent systems is its RELATE syntax for typed edges. Rather than encoding relationships as foreign keys in relational tables (which loses semantic meaning) or as adjacency lists in document fields (which makes traversal expensive), RELATE creates first-class edge records: `RELATE paper_a->cites->paper_b SET strength = 0.9`. These edges are queryable, typed, and traversable with graph path syntax. Combined with native vector field support for embedding storage, SurrealDB handles both the graph and vector layers of Cohezion's [[graphrag-knowledge-graph-with-surrealdb]] implementation.

The SurrealDB agent context schema stores agent sessions, tasks, decisions, and artifacts as interconnected records. Session nodes link to task nodes link to artifact nodes, enabling queries like "find all decisions made during sessions that produced high-coherence artifacts" — retrospective analytics that feed the [[experience-feedback-loop]]. The record-centric schema (as captured in [[lesson-surrealdb-schema-design]]) outperforms table-centric approaches by 60-70% in query complexity.

## Key Properties

- **Multi-model**: Document, relational, graph, and vector operations in one system
- **RELATE syntax**: First-class typed edge records with queryable metadata
- **SurrealQL**: SQL-familiar with graph path traversal and CONTAINS/SELECT FETCH extensions
- **Record IDs are typed**: IDs must match declared type at query time — a common source of bugs
- **Runs locally**: `ws://localhost:8000` with no cloud dependency; zero operational cost

## Definition

SurrealDB is a multi-model database that combines graph database capabilities, document storage, relational queries, and vector fields in a single system accessed through SurrealQL — a SQL-inspired query language with graph-native extensions. Unlike traditional databases that force a choice between document, relational, or graph models, SurrealDB handles all three simultaneously, making it well-suited for agent context graphs that need structured schema, relationship traversal, and vector similarity search.

SurrealDB's key differentiator for agent systems is its RELATE syntax for typed edges. Rather than encoding relationships as foreign keys in relational tables (which loses semantic meaning) or as adjacency lists in document fields (which makes traversal expensive), RELATE creates first-class edge records: `RELATE paper_a->cites->paper_b SET strength = 0.9`. These edges are queryable, typed, and traversable with graph path syntax. Combined with native vector field support for embedding storage, SurrealDB handles both the graph and vector layers of Cohezion's [[graphrag-knowledge-graph-with-surrealdb]] implementation.

The SurrealDB agent context schema stores agent sessions, tasks, decisions, and artifacts as interconnected records. Session nodes link to task nodes link to artifact nodes, enabling queries like "find all decisions made during sessions that produced high-coherence artifacts" — retrospective analytics that feed the [[experience-feedback-loop]]. The record-centric schema (as captured in [[lesson-surrealdb-schema-design]]) outperforms table-centric approaches by 60-70% in query complexity.

## Key Properties

- **Multi-model**: Document, relational, graph, and vector operations in one system
- **RELATE syntax**: First-class typed edge records with queryable metadata
- **SurrealQL**: SQL-familiar with graph path traversal and CONTAINS/SELECT FETCH extensions
- **Record IDs are typed**: IDs must match declared type at query time — a common source of bugs

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Obsidian's file recovery, version history, and local snapshots:

## File Recovery Plugin

To restore previous file versions, you can open the Obsidian Command Palette and run "File recovery: Open local history" to get a list of all the snapshots that exist for the current note.

## Local Snapshots

File Recovery snapshots are never synced because they're stored in global settings outside the vault's .obsidian folder. This means they remain on your local machine and are not synchronized through Obsidian Sync.

## Alternative Plugins

Several community plugins offer enhanced version history functionality:

1. **Time Machine Plugin**: The Time Machine plugin replaces the core File Recovery UI with something much more user-friendly, providing a visual timeline with diffs. It merges File Recovery snapshots and git commits into one timeline, allowing you to browse your note's full history regardless of whether a change was captured by Obsidian's auto-snapshot or by a manual git commit.

2. **Version Control Plugin**: This plugin focuses on manual, intentional snapshots where you decide the perfect moment to save a version and can give it a meaningful name like "Brainstorming complete" or "Final draft before rewrite".

## Key Approaches

### Metadata Formats

One approach involves saving markdown files with metadata using YAML format at the top, including fields like source, date_added, tags, category, and summary. Front matter can be placed at the beginning of markdown files to define properties such as title, author, date, and custom fields that documentation tools can use.

### Markdown vs JSON for Knowledge Bases

For AI-powered tools focused on data retrieval, JSON offers more reliability for structured data queries than Markdown, with the JSON format supporting more consistency and precision. However, some tools can convert documents into either clean Markdown or structured JSON depending on needs.

### Organizing Knowledge Bases

Categorizing Markdown files into folders and using simple metadata makes systems scalable, readable, and maintainable, enabling better navigation and user experience without requiring a full CMS.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SurrealDB features related to change feeds, record versioning, and temporal queries:

## Change Feeds

Change Feeds can record and replay any change to the database, following the Change Data Capture pattern. Change Feeds work by first defining a CHANGEFEED and its duration for our table. Changes in the database, such as creating, updating, or deleting, are recorded and played back in another channel.

You can optionally append INCLUDE ORIGINAL to include info on the current record before a change took place, and you can show changes since a certain date or since a version number.

## Record Versioning

Versioned temporal tables enable the option to 'go back in time' when querying your data. See how data looked before changes were made, or restore to a particular point-in-time. Since SurrealKV supports historical/temporal querying, you can use the VERSION clause when selecting or creating data to access historical data.

## Temporal Queries

A meta::VERSION special constant is treated as a field of all records, and which returns the stored version timestamp/datetime of a given record. There's also an active proposal for temporal querying that would enable features like customizable retention policies that allow developers to set retention policies at the table or record level, automatically pruning old versions based on time/storage constraints.

## SurrealDB 3.0

New indexing delivers faster queries and higher throughput by answering more requests directly from indexes, with smarter planners, concurrent index updates, and richer index capabilities that reduce full table scans.

Now let me compile a comprehensive summary of the findings:

## Document Versioning for Obsidian Vaults - Research Findings

Based on my research, here are the **five main approaches** to document versioning in Obsidian vaults, with practical recommendations for your setup:

### 1. **Built-In Obsidian Options**

**File Recovery (Core Plugin)**
- **How it works:** Obsidian automatically snapshots edits locally at intervals, stored outside the vault in global settings (`.obsidian` folder is not synced)
- **Access:** Command Palette → "File recovery: Open local history" shows snapshots with timeline
- **Limitation:** Snapshots are local-only, lost if vault is moved/reset

**Version History (Obsidian Sync only)**
- **How it works:** If you use Obsidian Sync subscription, it maintains versions server-side
- **Access:** Note properties → Version History tab
- **Limitation:** Requires paid subscription, not suitable for git-backed vaults

**Better UX:** [Time Machine Plugin](https://www.dsebastien.net/never-lose-a-note-again-time-machine-plugin-for-obsidian/) merges File Recovery snapshots + git commits into one unified timeline with diffs

---

### 2. **Git-Based Versioning (BEST FOR YOUR SETUP)**

**Obsidian Git Plugin** ([Vinzent03/obsidian-git](https://github.com/Vinzent03/obsidian-git))
- **How it works:** Integrates git directly into Obsidian—auto-commit on interval, view history in sidebar, diff viewer
- **Advantages:** 
  - Full commit history with messages
  - Works seamlessly with your existing repo on `track-c`
  - Integrates with your MCP server (can query git history)
  - Non-destructive (commits never overwrite untracked changes)
- **Ideal for:** Your vault since it's already a git repo

**Specialized Git Plugins:**
- [obsidian-git-changelog](https://github.com/shumadrid/obsidian-git-changelog) - Display dynamic changelogs by reading git history
- [Version History Diff Plugin](https://github.com/kometenstaub/obsidian-version-history-diff) - Side-by-side diff viewer for git versions

**Recommendation:** Use **git + Time Machine Plugin** combo:
- Git commits provide durable, auditable history
- Time Machine provides user-friendly timeline UI
- Both integrated into your existing workflow

---

### 3. **Local Snapshot-Based Versioning**

**Version Control Plugin** ([micmejia/obsidian-Version-Control](https://github.com/micmejia/obsidian-Version-Control))
- **How it works:** Manual, intentional snapshots saved locally (you decide when to snapshot with meaningful names like "Draft complete")
- **Advantages:**
  - Fine-grained control over history (no auto-snapshots of every keystroke)
  - Human-readable version names
  - In-file branching, timeline search
  - All local (no syncing issues)
- **Limitation:** Manual workflow, not suited for continuous tracking

**Use case:** Complementary to git for high-stakes edits (e.g., "Before major rewrite")

---

### 4. **JSON/Metadata-Based Versioning**

**Approach:** Add frontmatter metadata to track versioning info:
```yaml
---
title: Note Title
date: 2026-02-19
status: active
tags: [decision, architecture]
version: 2
version_history:
  - {version: 1, date: 2026-02-18, author: user, change: "Initial draft"}
  - {version: 2, date: 2026-02-19, author: user, change: "Added examples"}
---
```

**Advantages:**
- Self-documenting (version info embedded in file)
- Parseable by MCP server for programmatic queries
- Works with any vault structure
- Can reference git commit hashes in metadata

**Limitation:** Manual maintenance (you update metadata when versioning)

**Your MCP server could:**
- Query notes by version range
- Generate version reports
- Compare versions across papers
- Track when concepts evolved

---

### 5. **SurrealDB Temporal/Versioning Features** (Advanced)

**SurrealDB 3.0 capabilities for versioning:**

**Change Feeds:**
- Record all CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE events on tables
- Play back changes in order with `INCLUDE ORIGINAL` to see pre-change state
- Query changes since a specific date or version number
```surrealql
-- Define changefeed for vault notes
DEFINE TABLE notes SCHEMAFULL CHANGEFEED 7d;

-- Get all changes since a date
SELECT * FROM vault::changes WHERE time > 2026-02-19;
```

**Temporal/Versioned Tables:**
- Built-in versioning: `VERSION` clause enables "go back in time" queries
- `meta::VERSION` special field returns version timestamp
- Retention policies auto-prune old versions based on time/storage
```surrealql
-- Query historical state of a note
SELECT * FROM notes VERSION AT '2026-02-18T10:00:00Z';

-- Restore to a point-in-time
UPDATE notes SET status = 'active' VERSION AT '2026-02-18';
```

**Advantages:**
- Production-grade versioning with retention policies
- Efficient temporal queries without manually maintaining history
- Integrates with your SurrealDB instance (port 8360)
- MCP server can expose temporal queries as tools

**Limitation:** Requires SurrealKV backend (more complex setup); overkill for simple markdown versioning

---

### **Practical Recommendation for Your Vault**

**Tier 1 (Implement first):**
1. **Obsidian Git Plugin** — Leverage your existing git repo for durable history
2. **Time Machine Plugin** — User-friendly UI on top of git history + File Recovery snapshots
3. **One-line git commit policy** — Standardize messages: `Note: <title> - <change type>` (e.g., `Note: SurrealDB - Add temporal queries section`)

**Tier 2 (Optional enhancements):**
- **Version metadata in frontmatter** — Add `last_revised: YYYY-MM-DD` and `version_count: N` for MCP queries
- **Git tag markers** — Tag important milestones: `git tag v1.0-concepts` when concept suite stabilizes
- **Changelog aggregation** — Use `obsidian-git-changelog` to generate dynamic vault changelog

**Tier 3 (Future, if needed):**
- **SurrealDB Change Feeds** — If you need queryable version history across hundreds of notes
- **Version Control Plugin** — For high-stakes decisions (manual snapshots with intent)

---

### **Sources**
- [Obsidian Git Plugin](https://github.com/Vinzent03/obsidian-git)
- [File Recovery - Obsidian Help](https://help.obsidian.md/plugins/file-recovery)
- [Version History - Obsidian Help](https://help.obsidian.md/Obsidian+Sync/Version+history)
- [Time Machine Plugin - DSébastien](https://www.dsebastien.net/never-lose-a-note-again-time-machine-plugin-for-obsidian/)
- [Git Changelog Plugin](https://github.com/shumadrid/obsidian-git-changelog)
- [Version Control Plugin](https://github.com/micmejia/obsidian-Version-Control)
- [SurrealDB Features - Change Feeds](https://surrealdb.com/learn/fundamentals/schemafull/define-table)
- [SurrealDB Temporal Querying](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/issues/4860)
- [Markdown Knowledge Base with Metadata](https://www.datafuel.dev/blog/markdown-knowledge-base)

---
title: "Vault as System of Record — Store All System Definitions in the Vault"
date: 2026-03-05
status: proposed
tags: [decision, architecture, vault-architecture, disaster-recovery, compound-engineering]
aliases: ["vault system of record", "vault as SoR", "vault reconstruction manual"]
---

# Vault as System of Record

> [!danger] The Problem
> If the git repo is lost, or an agent session crashes, or MCP config is corrupted — can we rebuild? Today the answer is "partially." Skills live in `.claude/skills/`, agent rules in `.claude/rules/`, MCP config in `~/.claude/mcp.json`, tools in `tools/`. None of this is in the vault's knowledge graph. If the repo is gone, the vault has concepts and papers but not the instructions for how the system operates.

## Context

The vault currently stores **knowledge** (concepts, papers, decisions, lessons) but not **system definitions** (skills, agents, MCP servers, tools, hooks). These system definitions are the operating instructions that make the knowledge useful. Without them, an agent reading the vault can understand *what* Cohezion knows but not *how* Cohezion works.

| Asset | Current Location | In Vault? | Queryable? |
|-------|-----------------|-----------|------------|
| Skills | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` | No | No |
| Agent rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` | No | No |
| MCP servers | `~/.claude/mcp.json`, `.mcp.json` | No | No |
| Tools (CLI) | `tools/cohezion-engine/` | Code only | No |
| Hooks | `.claude/hooks/*.sh` | No | No |
| Agent definitions | Scattered in skills/rules | No | No |
| PRDs / Architecture | Sometimes ad-hoc | Partially | No |

## Decision

> [!tip] Proposed
> **Mirror all system definitions into the vault as structured notes.** The vault becomes the single source of truth for reconstructing the entire Cohezion system — not just the knowledge, but the machinery.

### What Gets Stored

| Asset Type | Vault Location | Format | Update Trigger |
|-----------|----------------|--------|----------------|
| **Skills** | `specs/skills/<name>.md` | Skill spec: purpose, triggers, steps, examples | After `/sync` or skill creation |
| **Agent Definitions** | `specs/agents/<name>.md` | Agent spec: role, tools, constraints, prompts | After agent design changes |
| **MCP Servers** | `specs/mcp-servers/<name>.md` | Server spec: URL, tools, auth, examples | After MCP config changes |
| **Tools** | `specs/tools/<name>.md` | Tool spec: commands, flags, examples, install | After tool releases |
| **Hooks** | `specs/hooks/<name>.md` | Hook spec: trigger, logic, alerts, cooldown | After hook modifications |
| **Workflows** | `specs/workflows/<name>.md` | Workflow spec: phases, gates, transitions | After workflow changes |

### Directory Structure

```
specs/
├── _index.md              ← Directory index with conventions
├── skills/
│   ├── vault-keeper.md    ← Mirrors .claude/skills/vault-keeper/SKILL.md
│   ├── daily-research.md
│   ├── flesh-out.md
│   ├── link.md
│   ├── note.md
│   └── triage.md
├── agents/
│   ├── plan-verifier.md
│   ├── plan-challenger.md
│   ├── spec-reviewer-compliance.md
│   └── spec-reviewer-quality.md
├── mcp-servers/
│   ├── cloud-vault-mcp.md
│   ├── ollama-mcp.md
│   ├── context7.md
│   ├── web-search.md
│   └── web-fetch.md
├── tools/
│   ├── cohezion-engine-cli.md
│   ├── vault-keeper-hook.md
│   └── mcp-cli.md
└── workflows/
    ├── spec-driven-development.md
    ├── compound-engineering.md
    └── vault-keeper-maintenance.md
```

### Document Versioning Strategy

> [!tip] Three-Tier Versioning
> Git for history, frontmatter for metadata, SurrealDB for temporal queries.

**Tier 1 — Git (durable history, already running):**
- Every vault change is a git commit on `track-c`
- `git log --follow specs/skills/vault-keeper.md` shows full evolution
- Git tags mark stable milestones: `git tag v1.0-skills`

**Tier 2 — Frontmatter metadata (self-documenting):**
```yaml
---
title: "Vault Keeper Skill"
date: 2026-03-05
version: 3
last_revised: 2026-03-05
revision_history:
  - {v: 1, date: 2026-03-04, change: "Initial skill creation"}
  - {v: 2, date: 2026-03-05, change: "Added Read mode, canvas nudge"}
  - {v: 3, date: 2026-03-05, change: "Added callout and alias nudges"}
tags: [spec, skill, vault-keeper]
---
```

**Tier 3 — SurrealDB temporal queries (queryable history):**
```surql
-- Define changefeed on specs table
DEFINE TABLE spec CHANGEFEED 90d;

-- Query: what changed in the last week?
SELECT * FROM spec WHERE synced_at > time::now() - 7d ORDER BY synced_at DESC;

-- Future: temporal queries when SurrealDB supports VERSION AT
```

### How Versioning Flows

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Agent edits spec note] -->|PostToolUse hook| B[Change Journal]
    A -->|git commit| C[Git History]
    B -->|Sync Daemon| D[SurrealDB record]
    D -->|Change Feed| E[Temporal Query]
    C -->|git log| F[Full History]
```

| Need | Tool |
|------|------|
| "What did this spec look like last week?" | `git show HEAD~5:specs/skills/vault-keeper.md` |
| "Which specs changed today?" | `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 specs/` |
| "Show me all skill versions" | SurrealDB query on `spec` table with changefeed |
| "What's the current version?" | Read frontmatter `version:` field |

## Consequences

> [!success] If Accepted
> - **Disaster recovery:** The vault alone is enough to rebuild the entire system — skills, agents, MCP config, tools, hooks, workflows
> - **Traceability:** Every system change is tracked (git + frontmatter + SurrealDB)
> - **Agent onboarding:** New agents read `specs/` to understand what tools and skills are available
> - **Cross-agent compatibility:** Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Codex agents can read `specs/` to understand the system
> - **Compound value:** System definitions participate in the knowledge graph — linked to concepts, decisions, and lessons

> [!warning] Maintenance Cost
> - Specs must stay in sync with actual `.claude/` config — stale specs are worse than no specs
> - Mitigation: `/sync` skill already exists; extend it to write vault specs as part of the sync cycle
> - Mitigation: vault-keeper hook can detect stale specs (compare `.claude/` timestamps vs `specs/` timestamps)

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Rejected Because |
|-------------|-----------------|
| **Just keep `.claude/` in git** | Hidden from knowledge graph, not queryable, not cross-linked |
| **Store in `patterns/`** | Patterns are reusable solutions, not system definitions — different lifecycle |
| **Store in `docs/`** | Docs is long-form prose, not structured specs |
| **Don't mirror, just reference** | References break when config changes; vault needs self-contained copy |

## Related

- [[2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline]] — The sync pipeline that makes SurrealDB versioning possible
- [[2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture]] — Architecture for vault↔SurrealDB communication
- [[compound-engineering]] — System definitions compound just like knowledge
- [[implementation-first-infrastructure-later]] — Start with manual specs, automate sync later
- [[non-blocking-observability]] — Versioning is observability of system evolution
- [[adversarial-review]] — Stale specs are a failure mode adversarial review should catch

purpose: "System definitions for skills, agents, MCP servers, tools, hooks, and workflows"

# Specs — System Definitions

**Purpose:** The vault's reconstruction manual. Everything an agent (or human) needs to rebuild the Cohezion system from scratch — skills, agents, MCP servers, tools, hooks, workflows, and IDE/model integrations.

> [!danger] Why This Exists
> If the repo is lost, if MCP config is corrupted, if `.claude/` is wiped — these specs are the blueprint for reconstruction. Every system definition lives here as a structured, cross-linked, versioned vault note.

**Put here when:** You create, modify, or document a system-level component (skill, agent, MCP server, tool, hook, workflow, or integration).

## Subdirectories

| Subdirectory | Contents | Naming |
|-------------|----------|--------|
| `skills/` | Skill specs — purpose, triggers, steps, examples | `<skill-name>.md` |
| `agents/` | Agent definitions — role, tools, constraints, prompts | `<agent-name>.md` |
| `mcp-servers/` | MCP server specs — URL, tools catalog, auth, examples | `<server-name>.md` |
| `tools/` | Tool specs — commands, flags, install, examples | `<tool-name>.md` |
| `hooks/` | Hook specs — trigger, logic, alerts, cooldown | `<hook-name>.md` |
| `workflows/` | Workflow specs — phases, gates, transitions | `<workflow-name>.md` |
| `integrations/` | IDE and model provider integration points | `<integration-name>.md` |

## Required Frontmatter

```yaml
---
title: "Component Name"
date: 2026-03-05
version: 1
last_revised: 2026-03-05
tags: [spec, <type>]  # type = skill | agent | mcp-server | tool | hook | workflow | integration
source: ".claude/skills/vault-keeper/SKILL.md"  # path to canonical source
status: active  # active | deprecated | draft
---
```

## Versioning Convention

- `version:` increments on every significant change
- `last_revised:` updates on any edit
- `revision_history:` optional array of `{v, date, change}` entries
- Git history provides full diff trail: `git log --follow specs/<path>`

## Sync Protocol

1. After modifying a skill/agent/tool → update the corresponding spec note
2. `/sync` skill writes vault specs as part of the sync cycle
3. Vault-keeper can detect stale specs (source timestamp > spec timestamp)

## Related

- [[2026-03-05-vault-as-system-of-record]] — ADR establishing this directory's purpose
- [[compound-engineering]] — System definitions compound like knowledge

# Vault Keeper Skill

> [!abstract] Purpose
> Autonomous maintenance agent that keeps the vault healthy, dense, navigable, and agent-readable. Orchestrates five specialist skills (vault-health, link, flesh-out, triage, note) in a single prioritized workflow.

## Invocation

```
/vault-keeper                    # Full maintenance cycle
/vault-keeper --quick            # Read-only health check (30 seconds)
/vault-keeper --triage           # Process inbox only
/vault-keeper --densify          # Link + flesh-out cycle
/vault-keeper --moc              # Generate/update Maps of Content
/vault-keeper --context "query"  # Load relevant vault context
```

## Proactive Behavior

The vault keeper fires automatically via PostToolUse hooks:

| Trigger | Cooldown | Checks |
|---------|----------|--------|
| Write/Edit on `.md` | 60 seconds | Inbox count, frontmatter, inbound links, canvas nudge, callout nudge, alias nudge |
| Read on `.md` | 5 minutes | Inbox count only (vault-wide pulse) |

## 6-Phase Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Phase 1: TRIAGE] --> B[Phase 2: AUDIT]
    B --> C[Phase 3: HEAL]
    C --> D[Phase 4: DENSIFY]
    D --> E[Phase 5: NAVIGATE]
    E --> F[Phase 6: REPORT]
```

| Phase | Purpose | Actions |
|-------|---------|---------|
| 1. TRIAGE | Zero inbox | Classify → research → structure → move → link |
| 2. AUDIT | Find issues | Broken links, orphans, frontmatter, thin notes, under-connected hubs |
| 3. HEAL | Fix issues | Add frontmatter, connect orphans, fix broken links |
| 4. DENSIFY | Expand + connect | Flesh out thin notes, add missing cross-links |
| 5. NAVIGATE | MOC generation | Create/update Maps of Content |
| 6. REPORT | Metrics | Before/after delta table |

## Quality Invariants

- 0 orphan notes in content directories
- 0 frontmatter issues
- 0 actionable broken links
- < 10% thin notes per directory
- 8+ Maps of Content
- 6+ avg wiki-links per note

## Hook Source

**File:** `.claude/hooks/vault-keeper-check.sh`

6 checks: inbox count, frontmatter validation, inbound link check, canvas nudge (10+ outbound links), callout nudge (decisions/lessons/patterns), alias nudge (concepts without aliases).

# Cohezion Engine CLI (`cz`)

> [!abstract] Purpose
> Workflow CLI for session management, context monitoring, worktree isolation, and plan lifecycle. Installed at `~/.local/bin/cz`.

## Install

```bash
cd tools/cohezion-engine && uv pip install -e .
```

## Commands

### Session & Context

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz context --json` | Get context usage percentage (OK/WARNING/CLEAR_NEEDED) |
| `cz session status --json` | Show session ID and directory |
| `cz session send-clear <plan.md>` | Trigger continuation with plan context |
| `cz session send-clear --general` | Trigger continuation without plan |

### Worktree Management

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz worktree detect --json <slug>` | Check if worktree exists |
| `cz worktree create --json <slug>` | Create worktree on new branch |
| `cz worktree diff --json <slug>` | List changed files vs base |
| `cz worktree sync --json <slug>` | Squash merge to base branch |
| `cz worktree cleanup --json <slug>` | Remove worktree and branch |
| `cz worktree status --json` | Show active worktree |

### Plan Lifecycle

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz plan register <path> <status>` | Associate plan with session |
| `cz plan status --json` | Show current plan |

### Status

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz status --json` | Version and config dir |
| `cz --version` | Version number |

## Session Identity

- Uses `COHEZION_SESSION_ID` env var (falls back to `pid-<PID>`)
- Session directory: `~/.cohezion-engine/sessions/<id>/`
- Continuation file: `~/.cohezion-engine/sessions/<id>/continuation.md`

|------|---------|

| `surrealdb_import_papers` | Bulk import papers/ to SurrealDB |
| `surrealdb_import_concepts` | Bulk import concepts/ to SurrealDB |
| `surrealdb_start_watching` | Start file watcher for real-time sync |
| `surrealdb_stop_watching` | Stop file watcher |

### Agent Context

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `agent_start_session` | Create agent session node in SurrealDB |
| `agent_log_decision` | Log a decision with reasoning chain |
| `agent_log_artifact` | Log an artifact produced by agent |

### Health

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/health` endpoint | Returns status of vault, SurrealDB, Ollama, disk, memory |

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Port | Service |
|------------|------|---------|
| SurrealDB 3.0 | 8000 | `cohezion-surreal.service` |
| Ollama | 11434 | `ollama.service` |
| Vault filesystem | — | `/home/mike-anderson/vaults/cohezion-vault` |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `MCP_API_KEY` | — | Bearer token auth |

| `SURREALDB_USERNAME` | `root` | SurrealDB auth |
| `SURREALDB_PASSWORD` | `root` | SurrealDB auth |
| `SURREALDB_NAMESPACE` | `cohezion` | SurrealDB namespace |
| `SURREALDB_DATABASE` | `vault` | SurrealDB database |
| `OLLAMA_URL` | `http://localhost:11434` | Ollama endpoint |

```bash
cd ~/dev/cohezion/cloud-vault-mcp
uv pip install -e .

systemctl --user start cohezion-vault.service
```

## Proactive Behavior

The vault keeper fires automatically via PostToolUse hooks:

| Trigger | Cooldown | Checks |
|---------|----------|--------|

```mermaid

    B --> C[Phase 3: HEAL]
    C --> D[Phase 4: DENSIFY]
    D --> E[Phase 5: NAVIGATE]

|-------|---------|---------|

| 2. AUDIT | Find issues | Broken links, orphans, frontmatter, thin notes, under-connected hubs |
| 3. HEAL | Fix issues | Add frontmatter, connect orphans, fix broken links |
| 4. DENSIFY | Expand + connect | Flesh out thin notes, add missing cross-links |
| 5. NAVIGATE | MOC generation | Create/update Maps of Content |
| 6. REPORT | Metrics | Before/after delta table |

- 0 orphan notes in content directories
- 0 frontmatter issues
- 0 actionable broken links
- < 10% thin notes per directory
- 8+ Maps of Content
- 6+ avg wiki-links per note

# Cohezion Engine CLI (`cz`)

> [!abstract] Purpose
> Workflow CLI for session management, context monitoring, worktree isolation, and plan lifecycle. Installed at `~/.local/bin/cz`.

## Install

```bash
cd tools/cohezion-engine && uv pip install -e .
```

## Commands

### Session & Context

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz context --json` | Get context usage percentage (OK/WARNING/CLEAR_NEEDED) |
| `cz session status --json` | Show session ID and directory |
| `cz session send-clear <plan.md>` | Trigger continuation with plan context |
| `cz session send-clear --general` | Trigger continuation without plan |

### Worktree Management

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz worktree detect --json <slug>` | Check if worktree exists |
| `cz worktree create --json <slug>` | Create worktree on new branch |
| `cz worktree diff --json <slug>` | List changed files vs base |
| `cz worktree sync --json <slug>` | Squash merge to base branch |
| `cz worktree cleanup --json <slug>` | Remove worktree and branch |
| `cz worktree status --json` | Show active worktree |

### Plan Lifecycle

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz plan register <path> <status>` | Associate plan with session |
| `cz plan status --json` | Show current plan |

### Status

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cz status --json` | Version and config dir |
| `cz --version` | Version number |

## Session Identity

- Uses `COHEZION_SESSION_ID` env var (falls back to `pid-<PID>`)
- Session directory: `~/.cohezion-engine/sessions/<id>/`
- Continuation file: `~/.cohezion-engine/sessions/<id>/continuation.md`

# Vault Manifest

**Read this first.** This file tells you where everything lives, where to put your output, and what conventions to follow.

## Directory Map

### Content Directories (where knowledge lives)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming | Required Frontmatter |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|---------------------|
| `concepts/` | Core definitions, frameworks, techniques | Defining a reusable idea, technology, or methodology | `kebab-case.md` (no date prefix) | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `papers/` | Research papers, articles, external sources | Summarizing external research with citations | `kebab-case-descriptive-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `decisions/` | Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) | Recording a choice with context, alternatives, consequences | `YYYY-MM-DD-decision-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `patterns/` | Reusable solutions and code patterns | Documenting a repeatable solution to a recurring problem | `kebab-case-pattern-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]` |
| `experiments/` | Hypothesis testing and results | Testing a hypothesis with method, results, learnings | `YYYY-MM-DD-experiment-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `projects/` | Project-level tracking and plans | Tracking a multi-session effort with goals and status | `YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | `title`, `date`, `status`, `tags[]` |
| `lessons/` | Lessons learned from mistakes/discoveries | Capturing something learned the hard way — prevents repeat mistakes | `kebab-case-lesson-title.md` | `title`, `date`, `tags[]`, `severity` |

### Workflow Directories (where work happens)

| Directory | Purpose | Put Here When... | Naming |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|--------|
| `inbox/` | Unsorted intake — triage point | Dropping raw ideas, unprocessed content, or agent output that needs classification | Any `.md` name |
| `daily/` | Daily notes, session logs, checkpoints | Recording a session's work, daily standup, or checkpoint | `YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` |
| `sessions/` | Formal session records with structured metadata | Documenting a compound engineering session with metrics | `session-NNN-*.md` |
| `missions/` | Multi-agent coordinated tasks | Orchestrating multiple agents toward a shared goal | `mission-name.md` or dated |
| `retrospectives/` | Post-session analysis | Reviewing what worked, what didn't, and why | `YYYY-MM-DD-retrospective.md` |
| `Agents/` | Agent execution records and walkthroughs | Storing agent run artifacts, traces, walkthroughs | `AgentName/UUID/` subdirs |

### Navigation Directories (how to find things)

| Directory | Purpose | Key Files |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `concepts/MOC-*.md` | Maps of Content — curated topic indexes | 8 MOCs: agentic-ai, quantum-physics, vault-architecture, platform-infrastructure, machine-learning, astrophysics, compound-engineering, safety-alignment |

### Infrastructure Directories (tooling, not content)

| Directory | Purpose | Agent Action |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `canvas/` | Standalone visual canvases (no companion note) | Create spatial maps, architecture diagrams |
| `teleport/` | Cloud-to-local file sync (tasks + results) | Use for cross-environment transfers |
| `docs/` | Long-form documentation, brand guides | Reference only — don't create here without asking |
| `meta/` | Self-recording, compound demos | Specialized — check before writing |
| `specs/` | Formal specifications | For major system designs |
| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

---

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/
I mapped relationships visually        → companion .canvas next to the .md, or canvas/ if standalone
I don't know where this goes          → inbox/     (always safe default)
```

### Project Artifacts — Store Everything in the Vault

> [!danger] Mandatory Rule
> **All project artifacts belong in the vault.** PRDs, architecture docs, epics, stories, and engineering specs are vault notes — not code repo files, not ephemeral chat output, not lost when context expires.

**Why:** The vault is disaster recovery for institutional memory. If the repo is lost, the vault preserves how to rebuild. If an agent session crashes, the vault preserves what was decided and why. Traceability lives here.

| Artifact | Where | Template |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **PRD / Product Requirements** | `projects/YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | Include: problem, success criteria, epics table, stories table, timeline |
| **Architecture Decision** | `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-architecture-name.md` | ADR template: context, decision, consequences, alternatives, diagrams |
| **Epic breakdown** | Section within the PRD note | Table with stories, estimates, priorities |
| **Story details** | Section within the PRD note, or separate `projects/YYYY-MM-DD-story-name.md` if large | Acceptance criteria, file references, blockers |
| **Spike / investigation** | `experiments/YYYY-MM-DD-spike-name.md` | Hypothesis, method, results, learnings |
| **Retrospective** | `retrospectives/YYYY-MM-DD-retro-name.md` | What worked, what didn't, actions |
| **Runbook / how-to** | `patterns/how-to-name.md` | Steps, prerequisites, troubleshooting |

**Cross-link rule:** Every architecture decision links to its parent PRD. Every PRD links to related concepts and lessons. Stories reference the files they'll change.

**Example structure for a project:**
```
projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline.md    ← PRD with epics + stories
decisions/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture.md    ← Architecture ADR
experiments/2026-03-05-sync-daemon-prototype.md          ← Spike results
lessons/lesson-health-check-must-test-auth.md            ← Lesson learned
retrospectives/2026-03-XX-sync-pipeline-retro.md         ← Post-project retro
```

**When in doubt, use `inbox/`.** The vault keeper triages inbox items into their proper location with correct frontmatter and cross-links.

---

## Canvas Files (Multimodal Assets)

**Notes explain. Canvases show.** When a topic has complex relationships, spatial layout reveals structure that prose cannot. Create `.canvas` files alongside their companion `.md` notes.

### When to Create a Canvas

| Signal | Canvas Type |
|--------|-------------|
| MOC with 10+ linked notes | **Relationship map** — nodes for notes, edges for connections |
| Architecture or system design | **Architecture diagram** — groups for layers, text cards for components |
| Decision with 3+ alternatives | **Decision landscape** — cards per option, edges to trade-offs |
| Research cluster spanning domains | **Domain map** — grouped by field, edges for cross-domain links |
| Vault keeper nudges you | The hook detected 10+ outbound links — the note wants a canvas |

### Naming and Placement

Canvas files live **alongside their companion note**:
- `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.md` → `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.canvas`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.md` → `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.canvas`
- Standalone canvases (no companion note) → `canvas/` directory

### JSON Format

Obsidian canvas files are JSON with `nodes` and `edges`:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"unique-id", "type":"file", "file":"concepts/machine-learning.md", "x":0, "y":0, "width":250, "height":60},
    {"id":"label-1",   "type":"text", "text":"## Key Insight\n\nMarkdown content here", "x":300, "y":0, "width":300, "height":120, "color":"4"},
    {"id":"group-1",   "type":"group","label":"ML Cluster", "x":-50, "y":-50, "width":600, "height":250, "color":"2"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id":"edge-1", "fromNode":"unique-id", "toNode":"label-1", "label":"informs"}
  ]
}
```

**Node types:**
- `file` — link to a vault note (opens on click). Use `"file": "path/to/note.md"`
- `text` — inline markdown card. Use `"text": "## Title\n\nContent"`
- `group` — visual grouping box. Use `"label": "Group Name"`

**Colors:** `"1"` red, `"2"` orange, `"3"` yellow, `"4"` green, `"5"` cyan, `"6"` purple, or hex `"#RRGGGG"`

**Layout tips:** Use x/y grid spacing of ~300px horizontal, ~150px vertical. Groups should surround their children with ~50px padding.

---

## Rich Formats

Plain text is the floor, not the ceiling. Obsidian renders these natively — use them to make notes scannable, visual, and precise.

### Callouts

Structured highlights for decisions, warnings, key insights. **Use liberally.**

```markdown
> [!tip] Key Insight
> Context management is the primary bottleneck in multi-agent systems.

> [!warning] Consequences
> Removing this cache invalidates all downstream embeddings.

> [!danger] Known Failure
> Never call this API without rate limiting — see [[lesson-18-mock-live-services-in-tests]].

> [!example] Usage
> ```python
> result = engine.query("semantic search")
> ```

> [!abstract] Summary
> Three-sentence TL;DR of this paper or decision.
```

**All types:** `note`, `abstract`/`summary`/`tldr`, `info`, `tip`/`hint`, `success`/`done`, `question`/`faq`, `warning`/`caution`, `failure`/`missing`, `danger`/`error`, `bug`, `example`, `quote`/`cite`, `todo`

**Foldable:** Add `-` to collapse by default: `> [!warning]- Click to expand`

| Directory | Recommended Callouts |
|-----------|---------------------|
| `decisions/` | `> [!warning]` for consequences, `> [!tip]` for rationale |
| `lessons/` | `> [!danger]` for the mistake, `> [!success]` for the fix |
| `papers/` | `> [!abstract]` for summary, `> [!example]` for key findings |
| `concepts/` | `> [!tip]` for key properties, `> [!example]` for usage |
| `patterns/` | `> [!example]` for code, `> [!warning]` for anti-patterns |

### Mermaid Diagrams

Obsidian renders Mermaid natively in fenced code blocks. Use for architecture, workflows, and relationships.

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Agent] -->|queries| B[Cloud Vault MCP]
    B -->|returns| C[Relevant Notes]
    C -->|injected into| D[Agent Context]
    class A,B,C,D internal-link;
```
````

**Tip:** Add `class NodeName internal-link;` to make nodes clickable vault links.

| Signal | Diagram Type |
|--------|-------------|
| System with 3+ interacting components | `graph TD` (top-down flowchart) |
| Process with sequential steps | `graph LR` (left-right flow) |
| Time-ordered events | `sequenceDiagram` |
| State transitions | `stateDiagram-v2` |
| Timeline/roadmap | `timeline` |

### Math / LaTeX

Obsidian renders MathJax natively. Use for physics, ML, and quantitative papers.

```markdown
Inline: The loss function $L(\theta) = -\sum y_i \log \hat{y}_i$ converges at...

Block:
$$
E = mc^2 \quad \text{and} \quad F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}
$$
```

### Aliases

Alternative names for discoverability. Obsidian autocomplete suggests aliases when linking.

```yaml
---
title: "Context Management"
aliases: ["context engineering", "context window optimization", "prompt context"]
---
```

**When to add aliases:**
- Concept has common abbreviations (RAG, MCP, LLM)
- Topic is known by multiple names in different communities
- Note title uses a specific framing but the concept is broader

### Embeds (Transclusion)

Pull content from one note into another. Keeps notes atomic while composing views.

```markdown
![[note-name]]              # Embed entire note
![[note-name#Heading]]      # Embed one section
![[note-name#^block-id]]    # Embed one paragraph
![[image.png|300]]          # Embed image with width
![[document.pdf#page=3]]    # Embed PDF at specific page
```

**When to embed:** MOCs summarizing key sections, decisions referencing experiment results, patterns showing code from concept notes.

### Heading Links

Deep-link into specific sections of notes. More precise than whole-note links.

```markdown
[[context-management#Key Properties]]     # Link to a heading
[[lesson-04#Prevention]]                  # Link to a section
```

**When to use:** Cross-referencing specific evidence, linking to a particular section of a long note rather than the whole thing.

### Block References

Make any paragraph linkable by adding `^block-id` at the end.

```markdown
The key insight is that context quality matters more than quantity. ^key-insight
```

Then reference from anywhere: `[[context-management#^key-insight]]`

---

## Conventions

### Frontmatter (YAML)

Every note in a content directory MUST have frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: "Note Title"
date: 2026-03-04
tags: [tag1, tag2, tag3]
aliases: ["alt name", "abbreviation"]
---
```

**Tags are ALWAYS arrays** — never comma-separated strings.
**Aliases are optional but encouraged** on concepts with multiple names or abbreviations.

**Status values by directory:**
- `decisions/`: `proposed` → `accepted` → `deprecated` | `rejected`
- `experiments/`: `in-progress` → `complete` | `failed`
- `projects/`: `active` → `complete` → `archived`

### Cross-References

Use Obsidian wiki-links: `[[note-name]]`

- Use bare filename (no path prefix): `[[machine-learning]]` not `[[concepts/machine-learning]]`
- Link at first mention of a concept
- Every note should have 3+ outbound wiki-links
- Every new note must be linked FROM at least one existing note (no orphans)

### Templates

Directories with `_template.md` files: `decisions/`, `patterns/`, `experiments/`, `projects/`, `daily/`

Copy the template when creating a new note in these directories.

---

## Quick Start for Agents

### Starting a session:
1. Read this manifest (you're doing it now)
2. Check `inbox/` for items needing triage
3. Load the relevant MOC for your task: `concepts/MOC-*.md`
4. Check `lessons/` for past mistakes related to your task

### During your session:
5. Create notes in the correct directory per routing rules above
6. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to connect every new note to 1-3 existing notes
7. Use proper frontmatter with tags as arrays

### Ending a session:
8. Log session summary to `daily/YYYY-MM-DD-session-id.md`
9. If you discovered something reusable, add it to `lessons/` or `patterns/`
10. Any raw output that needs triage → `inbox/`

---

## Vault Health Invariants

A healthy vault maintains:
- **0 orphan notes** in content directories
- **0 frontmatter issues** (missing or malformed)
- **0 broken wiki-links** (pointing to non-existent notes)
- **< 10% thin notes** (under 3KB) per directory
- **8+ Maps of Content** covering major topic clusters
- **6+ wiki-links per note** on average

The `/vault-keeper` skill enforces these automatically.

---

| `benchmarks/` | Performance benchmarking | For measurement data |
| `research/` | Research guides and API specs | For structured research output |
| `templates/` | Note templates (anti-patterns, etc.) | Copy, don't modify |
| `tools/` | Cohezion engine CLI source | Code, not notes |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | 3D graph visualization plugin | Code, not notes |
| `mcp-server/` | MCP server source | Code, not notes |

---

## Output Routing Rules

**When you produce output, route it to the correct directory:**

```
I found a new technique/technology    → concepts/
I summarized external research        → papers/
I made an architectural choice        → decisions/
I documented a reusable solution      → patterns/
I tested a hypothesis                 → experiments/
I'm tracking a multi-session effort   → projects/
I learned something the hard way      → lessons/
I have raw/unstructured content       → inbox/     (vault keeper will triage)
I'm logging today's session work      → daily/
I ran a multi-agent mission           → missions/
I'm reviewing what worked/didn't      → retrospectives/
I mapped relationships visually        → companion .canvas next to the .md, or canvas/ if standalone
I don't know where this goes          → inbox/     (always safe default)
```

### Project Artifacts — Store Everything in the Vault

> [!danger] Mandatory Rule
> **All project artifacts belong in the vault.** PRDs, architecture docs, epics, stories, and engineering specs are vault notes — not code repo files, not ephemeral chat output, not lost when context expires.

**Why:** The vault is disaster recovery for institutional memory. If the repo is lost, the vault preserves how to rebuild. If an agent session crashes, the vault preserves what was decided and why. Traceability lives here.

| Artifact | Where | Template |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **PRD / Product Requirements** | `projects/YYYY-MM-DD-project-name.md` | Include: problem, success criteria, epics table, stories table, timeline |
| **Architecture Decision** | `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-architecture-name.md` | ADR template: context, decision, consequences, alternatives, diagrams |
| **Epic breakdown** | Section within the PRD note | Table with stories, estimates, priorities |
| **Story details** | Section within the PRD note, or separate `projects/YYYY-MM-DD-story-name.md` if large | Acceptance criteria, file references, blockers |
| **Spike / investigation** | `experiments/YYYY-MM-DD-spike-name.md` | Hypothesis, method, results, learnings |
| **Retrospective** | `retrospectives/YYYY-MM-DD-retro-name.md` | What worked, what didn't, actions |
| **Runbook / how-to** | `patterns/how-to-name.md` | Steps, prerequisites, troubleshooting |

**Cross-link rule:** Every architecture decision links to its parent PRD. Every PRD links to related concepts and lessons. Stories reference the files they'll change.

**Example structure for a project:**
```
projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline.md    ← PRD with epics + stories
decisions/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture.md    ← Architecture ADR
experiments/2026-03-05-sync-daemon-prototype.md          ← Spike results
lessons/lesson-health-check-must-test-auth.md            ← Lesson learned
retrospectives/2026-03-XX-sync-pipeline-retro.md         ← Post-project retro
```

**When in doubt, use `inbox/`.** The vault keeper triages inbox items into their proper location with correct frontmatter and cross-links.

---

## Canvas Files (Multimodal Assets)

**Notes explain. Canvases show.** When a topic has complex relationships, spatial layout reveals structure that prose cannot. Create `.canvas` files alongside their companion `.md` notes.

### When to Create a Canvas

| Signal | Canvas Type |
|--------|-------------|
| MOC with 10+ linked notes | **Relationship map** — nodes for notes, edges for connections |
| Architecture or system design | **Architecture diagram** — groups for layers, text cards for components |
| Decision with 3+ alternatives | **Decision landscape** — cards per option, edges to trade-offs |
| Research cluster spanning domains | **Domain map** — grouped by field, edges for cross-domain links |
| Vault keeper nudges you | The hook detected 10+ outbound links — the note wants a canvas |

### Naming and Placement

Canvas files live **alongside their companion note**:
- `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.md` → `concepts/MOC-agentic-ai.canvas`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.md` → `decisions/2026-03-05-pick-database.canvas`
- Standalone canvases (no companion note) → `canvas/` directory

### JSON Format

Obsidian canvas files are JSON with `nodes` and `edges`:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"unique-id", "type":"file", "file":"concepts/machine-learning.md", "x":0, "y":0, "width":250, "height":60},
    {"id":"label-1",   "type":"text", "text":"## Key Insight\n\nMarkdown content here", "x":300, "y":0, "width":300, "height":120, "color":"4"},
    {"id":"group-1",   "type":"group","label":"ML Cluster", "x":-50, "y":-50, "width":600, "height":250, "color":"2"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id":"edge-1", "fromNode":"unique-id", "toNode":"label-1", "label":"informs"}
  ]
}
```

**Node types:**
- `file` — link to a vault note (opens on click). Use `"file": "path/to/note.md"`
- `text` — inline markdown card. Use `"text": "## Title\n\nContent"`
- `group` — visual grouping box. Use `"label": "Group Name"`

**Colors:** `"1"` red, `"2"` orange, `"3"` yellow, `"4"` green, `"5"` cyan, `"6"` purple, or hex `"#RRGGGG"`

**Layout tips:** Use x/y grid spacing of ~300px horizontal, ~150px vertical. Groups should surround their children with ~50px padding.

---

## Rich Formats

Plain text is the floor, not the ceiling. Obsidian renders these natively — use them to make notes scannable, visual, and precise.

### Callouts

Structured highlights for decisions, warnings, key insights. **Use liberally.**

```markdown
> [!tip] Key Insight
> Context management is the primary bottleneck in multi-agent systems.

> [!warning] Consequences
> Removing this cache invalidates all downstream embeddings.

> [!danger] Known Failure
> Never call this API without rate limiting — see [[lesson-18-mock-live-services-in-tests]].

> [!example] Usage
> ```python
> result = engine.query("semantic search")
> ```

> [!abstract] Summary
> Three-sentence TL;DR of this paper or decision.
```

**All types:** `note`, `abstract`/`summary`/`tldr`, `info`, `tip`/`hint`, `success`/`done`, `question`/`faq`, `warning`/`caution`, `failure`/`missing`, `danger`/`error`, `bug`, `example`, `quote`/`cite`, `todo`

**Foldable:** Add `-` to collapse by default: `> [!warning]- Click to expand`

| Directory | Recommended Callouts |
|-----------|---------------------|
| `decisions/` | `> [!warning]` for consequences, `> [!tip]` for rationale |
| `lessons/` | `> [!danger]` for the mistake, `> [!success]` for the fix |
| `papers/` | `> [!abstract]` for summary, `> [!example]` for key findings |
| `concepts/` | `> [!tip]` for key properties, `> [!example]` for usage |
| `patterns/` | `> [!example]` for code, `> [!warning]` for anti-patterns |

### Mermaid Diagrams

Obsidian renders Mermaid natively in fenced code blocks. Use for architecture, workflows, and relationships.

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Agent] -->|queries| B[Cloud Vault MCP]
    B -->|returns| C[Relevant Notes]
    C -->|injected into| D[Agent Context]
    class A,B,C,D internal-link;
```
````

**Tip:** Add `class NodeName internal-link;` to make nodes clickable vault links.

| Signal | Diagram Type |
|--------|-------------|
| System with 3+ interacting components | `graph TD` (top-down flowchart) |
| Process with sequential steps | `graph LR` (left-right flow) |
| Time-ordered events | `sequenceDiagram` |
| State transitions | `stateDiagram-v2` |
| Timeline/roadmap | `timeline` |

### Math / LaTeX

Obsidian renders MathJax natively. Use for physics, ML, and quantitative papers.

```markdown
Inline: The loss function $L(\theta) = -\sum y_i \log \hat{y}_i$ converges at...

Block:
$$
E = mc^2 \quad \text{and} \quad F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}
$$
```

### Aliases

Alternative names for discoverability. Obsidian autocomplete suggests aliases when linking.

```yaml
---
title: "Context Management"
aliases: ["context engineering", "context window optimization", "prompt context"]
---
```

**When to add aliases:**
- Concept has common abbreviations (RAG, MCP, LLM)
- Topic is known by multiple names in different communities
- Note title uses a specific framing but the concept is broader

### Embeds (Transclusion)

Pull content from one note into another. Keeps notes atomic while composing views.

```markdown
![[note-name]]              # Embed entire note
![[note-name#Heading]]      # Embed one section
![[note-name#^block-id]]    # Embed one paragraph
![[image.png|300]]          # Embed image with width
![[document.pdf#page=3]]    # Embed PDF at specific page
```

**When to embed:** MOCs summarizing key sections, decisions referencing experiment results, patterns showing code from concept notes.

### Heading Links

Deep-link into specific sections of notes. More precise than whole-note links.

```markdown
[[context-management#Key Properties]]     # Link to a heading
[[lesson-04#Prevention]]                  # Link to a section
```

**When to use:** Cross-referencing specific evidence, linking to a particular section of a long note rather than the whole thing.

### Block References

Make any paragraph linkable by adding `^block-id` at the end.

```markdown
The key insight is that context quality matters more than quantity. ^key-insight
```

Then reference from anywhere: `[[context-management#^key-insight]]`

---

## Conventions

### Frontmatter (YAML)

Every note in a content directory MUST have frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: "Note Title"
date: 2026-03-04
tags: [tag1, tag2, tag3]
aliases: ["alt name", "abbreviation"]
---
```

**Tags are ALWAYS arrays** — never comma-separated strings.
**Aliases are optional but encouraged** on concepts with multiple names or abbreviations.

**Status values by directory:**
- `decisions/`: `proposed` → `accepted` → `deprecated` | `rejected`
- `experiments/`: `in-progress` → `complete` | `failed`
- `projects/`: `active` → `complete` → `archived`

### Cross-References

Use Obsidian wiki-links: `[[note-name]]`

- Use bare filename (no path prefix): `[[machine-learning]]` not `[[concepts/machine-learning]]`
- Link at first mention of a concept
- Every note should have 3+ outbound wiki-links
- Every new note must be linked FROM at least one existing note (no orphans)

### Templates

Directories with `_template.md` files: `decisions/`, `patterns/`, `experiments/`, `projects/`, `daily/`

Copy the template when creating a new note in these directories.

---

## Quick Start for Agents

### Starting a session:
1. Read this manifest (you're doing it now)
2. Check `inbox/` for items needing triage
3. Load the relevant MOC for your task: `concepts/MOC-*.md`
4. Check `lessons/` for past mistakes related to your task

### During your session:
5. Create notes in the correct directory per routing rules above
6. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to connect every new note to 1-3 existing notes
7. Use proper frontmatter with tags as arrays

### Ending a session:
8. Log session summary to `daily/YYYY-MM-DD-session-id.md`
9. If you discovered something reusable, add it to `lessons/` or `patterns/`
10. Any raw output that needs triage → `inbox/`

---

## Vault Health Invariants

A healthy vault maintains:
- **0 orphan notes** in content directories
- **0 frontmatter issues** (missing or malformed)
- **0 broken wiki-links** (pointing to non-existent notes)
- **< 10% thin notes** (under 3KB) per directory
- **8+ Maps of Content** covering major topic clusters
- **6+ wiki-links per note** on average

The `/vault-keeper` skill enforces these automatically.

---

| Need | Start Here |
|------|------------|
| Agent architecture & multi-agent systems | `[[MOC-agentic-ai]]` |

## Quick Orientation

**Read `VAULT_MANIFEST.md` first.** It maps every directory, explains output routing, and lists conventions. Each directory also has a `_index.md` with purpose, naming rules, and key notes.

**All project artifacts belong in the vault.** PRDs, architecture docs, epics, stories, and specs are vault notes — not ephemeral output. The vault is disaster recovery for institutional memory.

The vault maintains these invariants automatically:

# Cloud Vault MCP

The Cloud Vault MCP server is Cohezion's primary knowledge management and agent infrastructure interface, implemented as an HTTP [[mcp-model-context-protocol]] server running on port 8360. It exposes 30+ tools across six categories, providing AI agents with programmatic access to the Obsidian vault, SurrealDB graph database, Google Sheets, Ollama inference, and Teleport task management — all through a single standardized protocol.

The server implements three logical operation layers. **VaultOps** handles file-level vault operations: reading, writing, searching, and cross-linking notes. **CompoundOps** implements the compound engineering primitives: `vault_log_decision`, `vault_log_experiment`, `vault_extract_pattern`, and `vault_find_relevant_context` — the tools that make the [[experience-feedback-loop]] concrete. **ObsidianOps** manages the graph layer: backlinks, forward links, tags, and wiki-link validation. Together these layers turn the Obsidian vault from a passive note store into an active, queryable knowledge graph that agents can read from and write to during execution.

The server was built using FastMCP (Python) and serves as the reference template for additional MCP servers in the Cohezion ecosystem. The `cloud-vault-mcp/` directory is explicitly documented as the template to copy when building new MCP servers, carrying 87% token savings versus building from scratch. It runs alongside the Ollama MCP server (stdio, no port) and exposes a `/health` endpoint that monitors all five infrastructure dependencies.
